lectio8.lat:
23 Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem,
24 et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite, et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
25 Simíliter et cálicem, postquam cœnávit, dicens: Hic calix novum testaméntum est in meo sánguine: hoc fácite, quotiescúmque bibétis, in meam commemoratiónem.
26 Quotiescúmque enim manducábitis panem hunc, et cálicem bibétis, mortem Dómini annuntiábitis donec véniat.
lectio8.eng:
23 For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread.
24 And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.
25 In like manner also the chalice, after he had supped, saying: This chalice is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as often as you shall drink, for the commemoration of me.
26 For as often as you shall eat this bread, and drink the chalice, you shall show the death of the Lord, until he come.

responsory8.lat:
R. Una hora non potuístis vigiláre mecum, qui exhortabámini mori pro me?
* Vel Judam non vidétis, quómodo non dormit, sed festínat trádere me Judǽis.
V. Quid dormítis? súrgite, et oráte, ne intrétis in tentatiónem.
R. Vel Judam non vidétis, quómodo non dormit, sed festínat trádere me Judǽis.
responsory8.eng:
R. Could ye not watch with Me one hour, ye that called one on the other to die for Me?
* Or see ye not Judas, how that he sleepeth not, but maketh haste to betray Me to the Jews?
V. Why sleep ye? Rise, and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.
R. Or see ye not Judas, how that he sleepeth not, but maketh haste to betray Me to the Jews?

lectio9.lat:
27 Itaque quicúmque manducáverit panem hunc, vel bíberit cálicem Dómini indígne, reus erit córporis et sánguinis Dómini.
28 Probet autem seípsum homo: et sic de pane illo edat, et de cálice bibat.
29 Qui enim mandúcat et bibit indígne, judícium sibi mandúcat et bibit, non dijúdicans corpus Dómini.
30 Ideo inter vos multi infírmi et imbecílles, et dórmiunt multi.
31 Quod, si nosmetípsos dijudicarémus, non útique judicarémur.
32 Dum judicámur autem, a Dómino corrípimur, ut non cum hoc mundo damnémur.
33 Itaque, fratres mei, cum convenítis ad manducándum, ínvicem exspectáte.
34 Si quis ésurit, domi mandúcet: ut non in judícium conveniátis. Cétera autem, cum vénero, dispónam.
lectio9.eng:
27 Therefore whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.
28 But let a man prove himself: and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of the chalice.
29 For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.
30 Therefore are there many infirm and weak among you, and many sleep.
31 But if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.
32 But whilst we are judged, we are chastised by the Lord, that we be not condemned with this world.
33 Wherefore, my brethren, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
34 If any man be hungry, let him eat at home; that you come not together unto judgment. And the rest I will set in order, when I come.

responsory9.lat:
R. Senióres pópuli consílium fecérunt,
* Ut Jesum dolo tenérent, et occíderent: cum gládiis et fústibus exiérunt tamquam ad latrónem.
V. Collegérunt pontífices et pharisǽi concílium.
R. Ut Jesum dolo tenérent, et occíderent: cum gládiis et fústibus exiérunt tamquam ad latrónem.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Senióres pópuli consílium fecérunt, * Ut Jesum dolo tenérent, et occíderent: cum gládiis et fústibus exiérunt tamquam ad latrónem.
responsory9.eng:
R. The elders of the people consulted
* That they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill Him they came out, as against a thief, with swords and staves.
V. The chief Priests and the Pharisees gathered a council.
R. That they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill Him: they came out, as against a thief, with swords and staves.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. The elders of the people consulted * That they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill Him: they came out, as against a thief, with swords and staves.

oratio_matutinum.lat: Réspice, quǽsumus, Dómine, super hanc famíliam tuam, pro qua Dóminus noster Jesus Christus non dubitávit mánibus tradi nocéntium, et crucis subíre torméntum:
oratio_matutinum.eng:
Look down, we beseech thee, O Lord, on this thy family, for which our Lord Jesus Christ did not hesitate to be delivered up into the hands of wicked men, and to suffer the torment of the Cross.
Who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

ant_laudes.lat:
Justificéris, Dómine, * in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
Dóminus * tamquam ovis ad víctimam ductus est, et non apéruit os suum.
Contrítum est * cor meum in médio mei, contremuérunt ómnia ossa mea.
Exhortátus es * in virtúte tua, et in refectióne sancta tua, Dómine.
Oblátus est * quia ipse vóluit, et peccáta nostra ipse portávit.
ant_laudes.eng:
O Lord, Thou shalt be justified * when Thou speakest, and be clear when Thou art judged.
The Lord was brought as a lamb * to the slaughter, and He opened not His mouth.
Mine heart is broken within me * all my bones tremble.
O Lord, Thou hast spoken unto us * in thy strength, and in thy Holy Banquet.
He was offered up because He willed it * and He bore our sins.

versum_2.lat:
V. Homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi.
R. Qui edébat panes meos, ampliávit advérsum me supplantatiónem.
versum_2.eng:
V. Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted;
R. Which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.

ant_2.lat: Tráditor autem * dedit eis signum, dicens: Quem osculátus fúero, ipse est, tenéte eum.
ant_2.eng: Now he that betrayed Him * gave them a sign, saying: Whomsoever I shall kiss, That Same is He: hold Him fast.

ant_3.lat: Cenántibus autem illis * accépit Jesus panem, et benedíxit, ac fregit, dedítque discípulis suis.
ant_3.eng: And, as they were eating * Jesus took bread, and blessed, and broke it, and gave to His disciples.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Zelus domus tuæ * comédit me, et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: The zeal of thine house * hath eaten me up, and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Avertántur retrórsum, * et erubéscant, qui cógitant mihi mala.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Let them be turned backward * and put to confusion that desire my hurt.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Deus meus, * éripe me de manu peccatóris.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Deliver me, my God, * out of the hand of the wicked.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Liberávit Dóminus * páuperem a poténte, et ínopem, cui non erat adjútor.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Lord shall deliver * the needy from the strong: the poor also, that hath no helper.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Cogitavérunt ímpii, * et locúti sunt nequítiam: iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The ungodly think * and speak wickedness: they speak loftily concerning oppression.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Exsúrge, Dómine, * et júdica causam meam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: Arise, O Lord, * and judge my cause.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Dixi iníquis: * Nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: I said unto the wicked: * Speak not wickedness against God.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Terra trémuit * et quiévit, dum exsúrgeret in judício Deus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: The earth trembled * and was still, when God arose to judgment.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: In die tribulatiónis * meæ Deum exquisívi mánibus meis.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: In the day of my trouble * I sought God with my hands.

verses.lat: Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
verses.eng: Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

verses.lat: Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: et non est substántia.
verses.eng: I stick fast in the mire of the deep: and there is no sure standing.

verses.lat: Veni in altitúdinem maris: et tempéstas demérsit me.
verses.eng: I am come into the depth of the sea: and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.

verses.lat: Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
verses.eng: I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.

verses.lat: Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, qui odérunt me gratis.
verses.eng: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, who hate me without cause.

verses.lat: Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei injúste: quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
verses.eng: My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: then did I pay that which I took not away.

verses.lat: Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
verses.eng: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee.

verses.lat: Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, Dómine virtútum.
verses.eng: Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, the Lord of hosts.

verses.lat: Non confundántur super me qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
verses.eng: Let them not be confounded on my account, who seek thee, O God of Israel.

verses.lat: Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
verses.eng: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.

verses.lat: Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
verses.eng: I am become a stranger to my brethren, and an alien to the sons of my mother.

verses.lat: Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
verses.eng: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

verses.lat: Et opérui in jejúnio ánimam meam: et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
verses.eng: And I covered my soul in fasting: and it was made a reproach to me.

verses.lat: Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: et factus sum illis in parábolam.
verses.eng: And I made haircloth my garment: and I became a byword to them.

verses.lat: Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
verses.eng: They that sat in the gate spoke against me: and they that drank wine made me their song.

verses.lat: Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: tempus benepláciti, Deus.
verses.eng: But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

verses.lat: In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, in veritáte salútis tuæ:
verses.eng: In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.

verses.lat: Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
verses.eng: Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

verses.lat: Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
verses.eng: Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.

verses.lat: Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
verses.eng: Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

verses.lat: Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
verses.eng: And turn not away thy face from thy servant: for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.

verses.lat: Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: propter inimícos meos éripe me.
verses.eng: Attend to my soul, and deliver it: save me because of my enemies.

verses.lat: Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, et reveréntiam meam.
verses.eng: Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, and my shame.

verses.lat: In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
verses.eng: In thy sight are all they that afflict me; my heart hath expected reproach and misery.

verses.lat: Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
verses.eng: And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.

verses.lat: Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
verses.eng: And they gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

verses.lat: Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
verses.eng: Let their table become as a snare before them, and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.

verses.lat: Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
verses.eng: Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; and their back bend thou down always.

verses.lat: Effúnde super eos iram tuam: et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
verses.eng: Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

verses.lat: Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
verses.eng: Let their habitation be made desolate: and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.

verses.lat: Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
verses.eng: Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; and they have added to the grief of my wounds.

verses.lat: Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: et non intrent in justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: and let them not come into thy justice.

verses.lat: Deleántur de libro vivéntium: et cum justis non scribántur.
verses.eng: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; and with the just let them not be written.

verses.lat: Ego sum pauper et dolens: salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
verses.eng: I am poor and sorrowful: thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.

verses.lat: Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: et magnificábo eum in laude:
verses.eng: I will praise the name of God with a canticle: and I will magnify him with praise.

verses.lat: Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: córnua producéntem et úngulas.
verses.eng: And it shall please God better than a young calf, that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.

verses.lat: Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
verses.eng: Let the poor see and rejoice: seek ye God, and your soul shall live.

verses.lat: Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: et vinctos suos non despéxit.
verses.eng: For the Lord hath heard the poor: and hath not despised his prisoners.

verses.lat: Laudent illum cæli et terra, mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
verses.eng: Let the heavens and the earth praise him; the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.

verses.lat: Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: et ædificabúntur civitátes Juda.
verses.eng: For God will save Sion, and the cities of Juda shall be built up.

verses.lat: Et inhabitábunt ibi, et hereditáte acquírent eam.
verses.eng: And they shall dwell there, and acquire it by inheritance.

verses.lat: Et semen servórum ejus possidébit eam: et qui díligunt nomen ejus, habitábunt in ea.
verses.eng: And the seed of his servants shall possess it; and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

verses.lat: Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde: Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína.
verses.eng: O God, come to my assistance; O Lord, make haste to help me.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur, qui quærunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed that seek my soul:

verses.lat: Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame that desire evils to me:

verses.lat: Avertántur statim erubescéntes, qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: Deus, ádjuva me.
verses.eng: But I am needy and poor; O God, help me.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: Dómine, ne moréris.
verses.eng: Thou art my helper and my deliverer: O Lord, make no delay.

verses.lat: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: in justítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.
verses.eng: In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion: deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.

verses.lat: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, et salva me.
verses.eng: Incline thy ear unto me, and save me.

verses.lat: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: ut salvum me fácias,
verses.eng: Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: that thou mayst make me safe.

verses.lat: Quóniam firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum es tu.
verses.eng: For thou art my firmament and my refuge.

verses.lat: Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:
verses.eng: Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.

verses.lat: Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: Dómine, spes mea a juventúte mea.
verses.eng: For thou art my patience, O Lord: my hope, O Lord, from my youth.

verses.lat: In te confirmátus sum ex útero: de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.
verses.eng: By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: from my mother’s womb thou art my protector.

verses.lat: In te cantátio mea semper: tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adjútor fortis.
verses.eng: Of thee shall I continually sing: I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.

verses.lat: Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: tota die magnitúdinem tuam.
verses.eng: Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; thy greatness all the day long.

verses.lat: Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.
verses.eng: Cast me not off in the time of old age: when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.

verses.lat: Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.
verses.eng: For my enemies have spoken against me; and they that watched my soul have consulted together,

verses.lat: Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, † et comprehéndite eum: quia non est qui erípiat.
verses.eng: Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, for there is none to deliver him.

verses.lat: Deus, ne elongéris a me: Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.
verses.eng: O God, be not thou far from me: O my God, make haste to my help.

verses.lat: Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.

verses.lat: Ego autem semper sperábo: et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.
verses.eng: But I will always hope; and will add to all thy praise.

verses.lat: Os meum annuntiábit justítiam tuam: tota die salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; thy salvation all the day long.

verses.lat: Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, † introíbo in poténtias Dómini: Dómine, memorábor justítiæ tuæ solíus.
verses.eng: Because I have not known learning, I will enter into the powers of the Lord: O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.

verses.lat: Deus, docuísti me a juventúte mea: et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.
verses.eng: Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.

verses.lat: Et usque in senéctam et sénium: Deus, ne derelínquas me,
verses.eng: And unto old age and grey hairs: O God, forsake me not,

verses.lat: Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:
verses.eng: Until I shew forth thy arm to all the generation that is to come:

verses.lat: Poténtiam tuam, et justítiam tuam, Deus, † usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: Deus, quis símilis tibi?
verses.eng: Thy power, and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: O God, who is like to thee?

verses.lat: Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:
verses.eng: How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:

verses.lat: Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: et convérsus consolátus es me.
verses.eng: Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; and turning to me thou hast comforted me.

verses.lat: Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.
verses.eng: For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: O God, I will sing to thee with the harp,

verses.lat: Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: et ánima mea, quam redemísti.
verses.eng: My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; and my soul which thou hast redeemed.

verses.lat: Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur justítiam tuam: cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.
verses.eng: Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.

verses.lat: Deus, judícium tuum regi da: et justítiam tuam fílio regis:
verses.eng: Give to the king thy judgment, O God: and to the king’s son thy justice:

verses.lat: Judicáre pópulum tuum in justítia, et páuperes tuos in judício.
verses.eng: To judge thy people with justice, and thy poor with judgment.

verses.lat: Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: et colles justítiam.
verses.eng: Let the mountains receive peace for the people: and the hills justice.

verses.lat: Judicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: et humiliábit calumniatórem.
verses.eng: He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: and he shall humble the oppressor.

verses.lat: Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, in generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, throughout all generations.

verses.lat: Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
verses.eng: He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; and as showers falling gently upon the earth.

verses.lat: Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis: donec auferátur luna.
verses.eng: In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, till the moon be taken away.

verses.lat: Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
verses.eng: And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

verses.lat: Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: et inimíci ejus terram lingent.
verses.eng: Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: and his enemies shall lick the ground.

verses.lat: Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
verses.eng: The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:

verses.lat: Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: omnes gentes sérvient ei:
verses.eng: And all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him.

verses.lat: Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: et páuperem, cui non erat adjútor.
verses.eng: For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: and the needy that had no helper.

verses.lat: Parcet páuperi et ínopi: et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
verses.eng: He shall spare the poor and needy: and he shall save the souls of the poor.

verses.lat: Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
verses.eng: He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: and their names shall be honourable in his sight.

verses.lat: Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: tota die benedícent ei.
verses.eng: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: they shall bless him all the day.

verses.lat: Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus ejus: et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
verses.eng: And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.

verses.lat: Sit nomen ejus benedíctum in sǽcula: ante solem pérmanet nomen ejus.
verses.eng: Let his name be blessed for evermore: his name continueth before the sun.

verses.lat: Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
verses.eng: And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: all nations shall magnify him.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, qui facit mirabília solus:
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone doth wonderful things.

verses.lat: Et benedíctum nomen majestátis ejus in ætérnum: et replébitur majestáte ejus omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
verses.eng: And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.

verses.lat: Quam bonus Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde!
verses.eng: How good is God to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!

verses.lat: Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
verses.eng: But my feet were almost moved; my steps had wellnigh slipped.

verses.lat: Quia zelávi super iníquos, pacem peccatórum videns.
verses.eng: Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, seeing the prosperity of sinners.

verses.lat: Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
verses.eng: For there is no regard to their death, nor is there strength in their stripes.

verses.lat: In labóre hóminum non sunt, et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
verses.eng: They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men.

verses.lat: Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
verses.eng: Therefore pride hath held them fast: they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

verses.lat: Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
verses.eng: Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: they have passed into the affection of the heart.

verses.lat: Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
verses.eng: They have thought and spoken wickedness: they have spoken iniquity on high.

verses.lat: Posuérunt in cælum os suum: et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
verses.eng: They have set their mouth against heaven: and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

verses.lat: Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
verses.eng: Therefore will my people return here and full days shall be found in them.

verses.lat: Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, et si est sciéntia in excélso?
verses.eng: And they said: How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?

verses.lat: Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, obtinuérunt divítias.
verses.eng: Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world they have obtained riches.

verses.lat: Et dixi: Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum, et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
verses.eng: And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, and washed my hands among the innocent.

verses.lat: Et fui flagellátus tota die, et castigátio mea in matutínis.
verses.eng: And I have been scourged all the day; and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.

verses.lat: Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
verses.eng: If I said: I will speak thus; behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.

verses.lat: Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, labor est ante me:
verses.eng: I studied that I might know this thing, it is a labour in my sight:

verses.lat: Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
verses.eng: Until I go into the sanctuary of God, and understand concerning their last ends.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: dejecísti eos dum allevaréntur.
verses.eng: But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: when they were lifted up, thou hast cast them down.

verses.lat: Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.
verses.eng: How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity.

verses.lat: Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.
verses.eng: As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.

verses.lat: Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
verses.eng: For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.

verses.lat: Ut juméntum factus sum apud te: et ego semper tecum.
verses.eng: I am become as a beast before thee: and I am always with thee.

verses.lat: Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, et cum glória suscepísti me.
verses.eng: Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, and with thy glory thou hast received me.

verses.lat: Quid enim mihi est in cælo? et a te quid vólui super terram?
verses.eng: For what have I in heaven? and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?

verses.lat: Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

verses.lat: Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
verses.eng: For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.

verses.lat: Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
verses.eng: But it is good for me to adhere to my God, to put my hope in the Lord God:

verses.lat: Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, in portis fíliæ Sion.
verses.eng: That I may declare all thy praises, in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

verses.lat: Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
verses.eng: O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

verses.lat: Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, quam possedísti ab inítio.
verses.eng: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

verses.lat: Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
verses.eng: The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

verses.lat: Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
verses.eng: Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

verses.lat: Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
verses.eng: And they that hate thee have made their boasts, in the midst of thy solemnity.

verses.lat: Posuérunt signa sua, signa: et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
verses.eng: They have set up their ensigns for signs, and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

verses.lat: Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt jánuas ejus in idípsum: in secúri et áscia dejecérunt eam.
verses.eng: As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

verses.lat: Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
verses.eng: They have set fire to thy sanctuary: they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

verses.lat: Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
verses.eng: They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

verses.lat: Signa nostra non vídimus, jam non est prophéta: et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
verses.eng: Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: and he will know us no more.

verses.lat: Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
verses.eng: How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

verses.lat: Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, de médio sinu tuo in finem?
verses.eng: Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

verses.lat: Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
verses.eng: But God is our king before ages: he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

verses.lat: Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
verses.eng: Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

verses.lat: Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
verses.eng: Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

verses.lat: Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
verses.eng: Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

verses.lat: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
verses.eng: Thine is the day, and thine is the night: thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

verses.lat: Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
verses.eng: Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

verses.lat: Memor esto hujus, inimícus improperávit Dómino: et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
verses.eng: Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

verses.lat: Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
verses.eng: Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

verses.lat: Réspice in testaméntum tuum: quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
verses.eng: Have regard to thy covenant: for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

verses.lat: Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
verses.eng: Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, Deus, júdica causam tuam: memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
verses.eng: Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

verses.lat: Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
verses.eng: Forget not the voices of thy enemies: the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

verses.lat: Confitébimur tibi, Deus: confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
verses.eng: We will praise thee, O God: we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.

verses.lat: Narrábimus mirabília tua: cum accépero tempus, ego justítias judicábo.
verses.eng: We will relate thy wondrous works: when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.

verses.lat: Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: ego confirmávi colúmnas ejus.
verses.eng: The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: I have established the pillars thereof.

verses.lat: Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
verses.eng: I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.

verses.lat: Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
verses.eng: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not iniquity against God.

verses.lat: Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: for God is the judge.

verses.lat: Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
verses.eng: One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.

verses.lat: Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx ejus non est exinaníta: bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
verses.eng: And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: all the sinners of the earth shall drink.

verses.lat: Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: cantábo Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: But I will declare for ever: I will sing to the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: et exaltabúntur córnua justi.
verses.eng: And I will break all the horns of sinners: but the horns of the just shall be exalted.

verses.lat: Notus in Judǽa Deus: in Israël magnum nomen ejus.
verses.eng: In Judea God is known: his name is great in Israel.

verses.lat: Et factus est in pace locus ejus: et habitátio ejus in Sion.
verses.eng: And his place is in peace: and his abode in Sion:

verses.lat: Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, scutum, gládium, et bellum.
verses.eng: There hath he broken the powers of bows, the shield, the sword, and the battle.

verses.lat: Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
verses.eng: Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills. All the foolish of heart were troubled.

verses.lat: Dormiérunt somnum suum: et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.
verses.eng: They have slept their sleep; and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.

verses.lat: Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Jacob, dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.
verses.eng: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.

verses.lat: Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? ex tunc ira tua.
verses.eng: Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? from that time thy wrath.

verses.lat: De cælo audítum fecísti judícium: terra trémuit et quiévit,
verses.eng: Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: the earth trembled and was still,

verses.lat: Cum exsúrgeret in judícium Deus, ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.
verses.eng: When God arose in judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.

verses.lat: Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
verses.eng: For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.

verses.lat: Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: omnes, qui in circúitu ejus affértis múnera.
verses.eng: Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: all you that are round about him bring presents.

verses.lat: Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, terríbili apud reges terræ.
verses.eng: To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: to the terrible with the kings of the earth.

verses.lat: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: voce mea ad Deum, et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: I cried to the Lord with my voice; to God with my voice, and he gave ear to me.

verses.lat: In die tribulatiónis meæ Deum exquisívi, mánibus meis nocte contra eum: et non sum decéptus.
verses.eng: In the day of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night, and I was not deceived.

verses.lat: Rénuit consolári ánima mea, memor fui Dei, et delectátus sum, et exercitátus sum: et defécit spíritus meus.
verses.eng: My soul refused to be comforted: I remembered God, and was delighted, and was exercised, and my spirit swooned away.

verses.lat: Anticipavérunt vigílias óculi mei: turbátus sum, et non sum locútus.
verses.eng: My eyes prevented the watches: I was troubled, and I spoke not.

verses.lat: Cogitávi dies antíquos: et annos ætérnos in mente hábui.
verses.eng: I thought upon the days of old: and I had in my mind the eternal years.

verses.lat: Et meditátus sum nocte cum corde meo, et exercitábar, et scopébam spíritum meum.
verses.eng: And I meditated in the night with my own heart: and I was exercised and I swept my spirit.

verses.lat: Numquid in ætérnum proíciet Deus: aut non appónet ut complacítior sit adhuc?
verses.eng: Will God then cast off for ever? or will he never be more favourable again?

verses.lat: Aut in finem misericórdiam suam abscíndet, a generatióne in generatiónem?
verses.eng: Or will he cut off his mercy for ever, from generation to generation?

verses.lat: Aut obliviscétur miseréri Deus? aut continébit in ira sua misericórdias suas?
verses.eng: Or will God forget to shew mercy? or will he in his anger shut up his mercies?

verses.lat: Et dixi: Nunc cœpi: hæc mutátio déxteræ Excélsi.
verses.eng: And I said, Now have I begun: this is the change of the right hand of the most High.

verses.lat: Memor fui óperum Dómini: quia memor ero ab inítio mirabílium tuórum.
verses.eng: I remembered the works of the Lord: for I will be mindful of thy wonders from the beginning.

verses.lat: Et meditábor in ómnibus opéribus tuis: et in adinventiónibus tuis exercébor.
verses.eng: And I will meditate on all thy works: and will be employed in thy inventions.

verses.lat: Deus, in sancto via tua: quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster? tu es Deus qui facis mirabília.
verses.eng: Thy way, O God, is in the holy place: who is the great God like our God? Thou art the God that dost wonders.

verses.lat: Notam fecísti in pópulis virtútem tuam: redemísti in brácchio tuo pópulum tuum, fílios Jacob et Joseph.
verses.eng: Thou hast made thy power known among the nations: with thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people, the children of Jacob and of Joseph.

verses.lat: Vidérunt te aquæ, Deus, vidérunt te aquæ: et timuérunt, et turbátæ sunt abýssi.
verses.eng: The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee: and they were afraid, and the depths were troubled.

verses.lat: Multitúdo sónitus aquárum: vocem dedérunt nubes.
verses.eng: Great was the noise of the waters: the clouds sent out a sound.

verses.lat: Étenim sagíttæ tuæ tránseunt: vox tonítrui tui in rota.
verses.eng: For thy arrows pass: the voice of thy thunder in a wheel.

verses.lat: Illuxérunt coruscatiónes tuæ orbi terræ: commóta est, et contrémuit terra.
verses.eng: Thy lightnings enlightened the world: the earth shook and trembled.

verses.lat: In mari via tua, et sémitæ tuæ in aquis multis: et vestígia tua non cognoscéntur.
verses.eng: Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters: and thy footsteps shall not be known.

verses.lat: Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum, in manu Móysi et Aaron.
verses.eng: Thou hast conducted thy people like sheep, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

quad6-5.officium:
Feria Sexta in Parasceve

[Officium] (rubrica 1955 aut rubrica 196)
Feria Sexta in Passione et Morte Domini

ant_vespera.lat:
Cálicem * salutáris accípiam et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.
Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.
ant_vespera.eng:
I will take the cup of salvation; * and call upon the Name of the Lord.
With them * that hated peace I was peaceable: when I spoke to them they fought against me without cause.
From unjust men * deliver me, O Lord.
Keep me * from the snare, which they have laid for me, and from the stumbling-blocks of them that work iniquity.
I looked * on my right hand, and beheld, and there was no one that would know me.

oratio.lat: [Prelude Vespera] (rubrica 1955 aut rubrica 196)
oratio.eng: [Prelude Vespera] (rubrica 1955 aut rubrica 1960)

ant_matutinum.lat:
Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum, advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Divisérunt sibi * vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
Insurrexérunt in me * testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
Vim faciébant, * qui quærébant ánimam meam.
Confundántur * et revereántur, qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
Aliéni * insurrexérunt in me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.
Ab insurgéntibus in me * líbera me, Dómine, quia occupavérunt ánimam meam.
Longe fecísti * notos meos a me: tráditus sum, et non egrediébar.
Captábunt * in ánimam justi, et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
ant_matutinum.eng:
The kings of the earth set themselves, * and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against His Anointed.
They part my garments among them, * and cast lots upon my vesture.
False witnesses are risen up against me, * and iniquity hath belied itself.
They that sought after my life * have used violence again me.
Let them be ashamed and confounded * together that seek after my soul, to destroy it.
Strangers are risen up against me, * and oppressors seek after my soul.
O Lord, defend me from them that rise up against me, * for they lie in wait for my life.
Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; * I am shut up, and cannot come forth.
They gather themselves together * against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.

nocturn_1_versum.lat:
V. Divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea.
R. Et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
nocturn_1_versum.eng:
V. They part my garments among them.
R. And cast lots upon my vesture.

nocturn_2_versum.lat:
V. Insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui.
R. Et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
nocturn_2_versum.eng:
V. False witnesses are risen up against me.
R. And iniquity hath belied itself.

nocturn_3_versum.lat:
V. Locúti sunt advérsum me lingua dolósa.
R. Et sermónibus ódii circumdedérunt me, et expugnavérunt me gratis.
nocturn_3_versum.eng:
V. They have spoken against me with a lying tongue.
R. They compassed me about also with words of hatred, and fought against me without a cause.

lectio1.lat:
De Lamentatióne Jeremíæ Prophétæ
8 Heth. Cogitávit Dóminus dissipáre murum fíliæ Sion: teténdit funículum suum, et non avértit manum suam a perditióne: luxítque antemurále, et murus páriter dissipátus est.
9 Teth. Defíxæ sunt in terra portæ ejus: pérdidit, et contrívit vectes ejus: regem ejus et príncipes ejus in géntibus: non est lex, et prophétæ ejus non invenérunt visiónem a Dómino.
10 Jod. Sedérunt in terra, conticuérunt senes fíliæ Sion: conspersérunt cínere cápita sua, accíncti sunt cilíciis, abjecérunt in terram cápita sua vírgines Jerúsalem.
11 Caph. Defecérunt præ lácrimis óculi mei, conturbáta sunt víscera mea: effúsum est in terra jecur meum super contritióne fíliæ pópuli mei, cum defíceret párvulus et lactens in platéis óppidi.
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio1.eng:
Lesson from the book of Lamentations
8 Heth. The Lord hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Sion: he hath stretched out his line, and hath not withdrawn his hand from destroying: and the bulwark hath mourned, and the wall hath been destroyed together.
9 Teth. Her gates are sunk into the ground: he hath destroyed, and broken her bars: her king and her princes are among the Gentiles: the law is no more, and her prophets have found no vision from the Lord.
10 Jod. The ancients of the daughter of Sion sit upon the ground, they have held their peace: they have sprinkled their heads with dust, they are girded with haircloth, the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.
11 Caph. My eyes have failed with weeping, my bowels are troubled: my liver is poured out upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my people, when the children, and the sucklings, fainted away in the streets of the city.
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory1.lat:
R. Omnes amíci mei dereliquérunt me, et prævaluérunt insidiántes mihi: trádidit me quem diligébam:
* Et terribílibus óculis plaga crudéli percutiéntes, acéto potábant me.
V. Inter iníquos projecérunt me, et non pepercérunt ánimæ meæ.
R. Et terribílibus óculis plaga crudéli percutiéntes, acéto potábant me.
responsory1.eng:
R. All my friends have forsaken me, and mine enemies have prevailed against me; he whom I loved hath betrayed me.
* Mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me; he breaketh me with breach upon breach: and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
V. I am numbered with the transgressors; and my life is not spared.
R. Mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me; he breaketh me with breach upon breach; and (in my thirst) they gave me vinegar to drink.

lectio2.lat:
12 Lamed. Mátribus suis dixérunt: Ubi est tríticum et vinum? cum defícerent quasi vulneráti in platéis civitátis: cum exhalárent ánimas suas in sinu matrum suárum.
13 Mem. Cui comparábo te? vel cui assimilábo te, fília Jerúsalem? cui exæquábo te, et consolábor te, virgo fília Sion? Magna est enim velut mare contrítio tua: quis medébitur tui?
14 Nun. Prophétæ tui vidérunt tibi falsa et stulta, nec aperiébant iniquitátem tuam, ut te ad pœniténtiam provocárent: vidérunt autem tibi assumptiónes falsas, et ejectiónes.
15 Samech. Plausérunt super te mánibus omnes transeúntes per viam: sibilavérunt, et movérunt caput suum super fíliam Jerúsalem: Hǽccine est urbs, dicéntes, perfécti decóris, gáudium univérsæ terræ?
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio2.eng:
12 Lamed. They said to their mothers: Where is corn and wine? when they fainted away as the wounded in the streets of the city: when they breathed out their souls in the bosoms of their mothers.
13 Mem. To what shall I compare thee? or to what shall I liken thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? to what shall I equal thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Sion? for great as the sea is thy destruction: who shall heal thee?
14 Nun. thy prophets have seen false and foolish things for thee: and they have not laid open thy iniquity, to excite thee to penance: but they have seen for thee false revelations and banishments.
5 Samech. All they that passed by the way have clapped their hands at thee: they have hissed, and wagged their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying: Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of all the earth?
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory2.lat:
R. Velum templi scissum est,
* Et omnis terra trémuit: latro de cruce clamábat, dicens: Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
V. Petræ scissæ sunt, et monuménta apérta sunt, et multa córpora sanctórum, qui dormíerant, surrexérunt.
R. Et omnis terra trémuit: latro de cruce clamábat, dicens: Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
responsory2.eng:
R. The veil of the Temple was rent in twain, from the top to the bottom,
* And all the earth did quake: the thief on the cross cried, saying: Lord, remember me when Thou comest into thy kingdom!
V. The rocks rent, and the graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints, which slept, arose.
R. And all the earth did quake: the thief on the cross cried, saying: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

lectio3.lat:
1 Aleph. Ego vir videns paupertátem meam in virga indignatiónis ejus.
2 Aleph. Me minávit, et addúxit in ténebras, et non in lucem.
3 Aleph. Tantum in me vertit, et convértit manum suam tota die.
4 Beth. Vetústam fecit pellem meam, et carnem meam, contrívit ossa mea.
5 Beth. Ædificávit in gyro meo, et circúmdedit me felle et labóre.
6 Beth. In tenebrósis collocávit me, quasi mórtuos sempitérnos.
7 Ghimel. Circumædificávit advérsum me, ut non egrédiar: aggravávit cómpedem meum.
8 Ghimel. Sed et, cum clamávero et rogávero, exclúsit oratiónem meam.
9 Ghimel. Conclúsit vias meas lapídibus quadris, sémitas meas subvértit.
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio3.eng:
1 Aleph. I am the man that see my poverty by the rod of his indignation.
2 Aleph. He hath led me, and brought me into darkness, and not into light.
3 Aleph. Only against me he hath turned, and turned again his hand all the day.
4 Beth. My skin and my flesh he hath made old, he hath broken my bones.
5 Beth. He hath built round about me, and he hath compassed me with gall and labour.
6 Beth. He hath set me in dark places as those that are dead for ever.
7 Ghimel. He hath built against me round about, that I may not get out: he hath made my fetters heavy.
8 Ghimel. Yea, and when I cry, and entreat, he hath shut out my prayer.
9 Ghimel. He hath shut up my ways with square stones, he hath turned my paths upside down
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory3.lat:
R. Vínea mea elécta, ego te plantávi:
* Quómodo convérsa es in amaritúdinem, ut me crucifígeres et Barábbam dimítteres?
V. Sepívi te, et lápides elégi ex te, et ædificávi turrim.
R. Quómodo convérsa es in amaritúdinem, ut me crucifígeres et Barábbam dimítteres?
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Vínea mea elécta, ego te plantávi: * Quómodo convérsa es in amaritúdinem, ut me crucifígeres et Barábbam dimítteres?
responsory3.eng:
R. I had planted thee a noble vineyard;
* How then art thou turned into a degenerate plant, which willest that Barabbas should be released unto thee, and that I should be crucified.
V. I fenced thee, and gathered out the stones from thee, and built a tower in the midst of the land.
R. How then art thou turned into a degenerate plant, which willest that Barabbas should be released unto thee, and that I should be crucified.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. I had planted thee a noble vineyard; * How then art thou turned into a degenerate plant, which willest that Barabbas should be released unto thee, and that I should be crucified.

lectio4.lat:
Ex tractátu sancti Augustíni Epíscopi super Psalmos
Protexísti me, Deus, a convéntu malignántium, a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem. Jam ipsum caput nostrum intueámur. Multi Mártyres tália passi sunt, sed nihil sic elúcet, quómodo caput Mártyrum: ibi mélius intuémur, quod illi expérti sunt. Protéctus est a multitúdine malignántium, protegénte se Deo, protegénte carnem suam ipso Fílio, et hómine, quem gerébat: quia fílius hóminis est, et Fílius Dei est. Fílius Dei, propter formam Dei: fílius hóminis, propter formam servi, habens in potestáte pónere ánimam suam, et recípere eam. Quid ei potuérunt fácere inimíci? Occidérunt corpus, ánimam non occidérunt. Inténdite. Parum ergo erat, Dóminum hortári Mártyres verbo, nisi firmáret exémplo.
lectio4.eng:
From the Treatise of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo,) Upon the Psalms
Thou hast hidden me from the secret counsel of the wicked, from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity. Now let us fix our eyes upon our Head. Many martyrs have suffered such things as He suffered, but God's hiding of His suffering servants is not so well seen in the Martyrs, as it is in the Captain of the Martyrs. And it is in Him that we best see how it fared with them. He was hidden from the secret counsel of the wicked; hidden by God, being Himself God; hidden, as touching the Manhood, by God the Son, and the very Manhood, Which is taken into God the Son; because He is the Son of man, and He is the Son of God; Son of God, as being in the form of God; Son of man, as having taken upon Him the form of a servant, (Phil. ii. 6, 7,) Whose life no man taketh from Him, but Who layeth it down of Himself. He hath power to lay it down, and He hath power to take it again, (John x. 18.) What then was all that they which hated Him could do? They could kill the Body, but they were not able to kill the Soul. Consider this very earnestly. It had been a small thing for the Lord to preach to the Martyrs by His word, if He had not also nerved them by His example.

responsory4.lat:
R. Tamquam ad latrónem exístis cum gládiis et fústibus comprehéndere me:
* Cotídie apud vos eram in templo docens, et non me tenuístis: et ecce flagellátum dúcitis ad crucifigéndum.
V. Cumque injecíssent manus in Jesum, et tenuíssent eum, dixit ad eos.
R. Cotídie apud vos eram in templo docens, et non me tenuístis: et ecce flagellátum dúcitis ad crucifigéndum.
responsory4.eng:
R. Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves, for to take Me?
* I sat daily with you, teaching in the Temple, and ye laid no hold on Me; and, now when ye have scourged Me, ye lead Me away to crucify Me!
V. And when they had laid hands on Jesus, and taken Him, He said unto them:
R. I sat daily with you, teaching in the Temple, and ye laid no hold on Me; and now, when ye have scourged Me, ye lead Me away to crucify Me!

lectio5.lat: Nostis qui convéntus erat malignántium Judæórum, et quæ multitúdo erat operántium iniquitátem. Quam iniquitátem? Quia voluérunt occídere Dóminum Jesum Christum. Tanta ópera bona, inquit, osténdi vobis: propter quod horum me vultis occídere? Pértulit omnes infírmos eórum, curávit omnes lánguidos eórum, prædicávit regnum cælórum, non tácuit vítia eórum, ut ipsa pótius eis displicérent, non médicus, a quo sanabántur. His ómnibus curatiónibus ejus ingráti, tamquam multa febre phrenétici, insaniéntes in médicum, qui vénerat curáre eos, excogitavérunt consílium perdéndi eum: tamquam ibi voléntes probáre, utrum vere homo sit, qui mori possit, an áliquid super hómines sit, et mori se non permíttat. Verbum ipsórum agnóscimus in Sapiéntia Salomónis: Morte turpíssima, ínquiunt, condemnémus eum. Interrogémus eum: erit enim respéctus in sermónibus illíus. Si enim vere Fílius Dei est, líberet eum.
lectio5.eng: We know what secret counsel was that of the wicked Jews, and what insurrection was that of the workers of iniquity. Of what iniquity were they the workers? The murder of our Lord Jesus Christ. Many good works, saith He, have I showed you for which of those works go ye about to kill Me? He had borne with all their weaknesses: He had healed all their diseases: He had preached unto them the kingdom of heaven: He had discovered to them their iniquities, that they might rather hate them, than the Physician That came to cure them. And now at last, without gratitude for all the tenderness of His healing love, like men raging in an high delirium, throwing themselves madly on the Physician, Who had come to cure them, they took counsel together how they might kill Him, as if to see if He were a Man and could die, or Something more than a man, and That would not let Himself die. In the Wisdom of Solomon we recognize their words, (ii. 18, 19, 20,) Let us condemn Him with a shameful death. Let us examine Him; for, by His own saying, He shall be respected. If He be the Son of God, let Him help Him.

responsory5.lat:
R. Ténebræ factæ sunt, dum crucifixíssent Jesum Judǽi: et circa horam nonam exclamávit Jesus voce magna: Deus meus, ut quid me dereliquísti?
* Et inclináto cápite, emísit spíritum.
V. Exclámans Jesus voce magna, ait: Pater, in manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum.
R. Et inclináto cápite, emísit spíritum.
responsory5.eng:
R. The Jews crucified Jesus: and there was darkness (over all the land, unto the ninth hour): and about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, (saying): My God, (My God,) why hast Thou forsaken Me?
* And He bowed His Head, and gave up the Ghost.
V. When Jesus had cried with a loud voice, He said: Father, into thy hands I commend My Spirit.
R. And He bowed His Head, and gave up the Ghost.

lectio6.lat: Exacuérunt tamquam gládium linguas suas. Non dicant Judǽi: Non occídimus Christum. Etenim proptérea eum dedérunt júdici Piláto, ut quasi ipsi a morte ejus videréntur immúnes. Nam cum dixísset eis Pilátus: Vos eum occídite: respondérunt, Nobis non licet occídere quemquam. Iniquitátem facínoris sui in júdicem hóminem refúndere volébant: sed numquid Deum júdicem fallébant? Quod fecit Pilátus, in eo ipso quod fecit, aliquántum párticeps fuit: sed in comparatióne illórum multo ipse innocéntior. Institit enim quantum pótuit, ut illum ex eórum mánibus liberáret: nam proptérea flagellátum prodúxit ad eos. Non persequéndo Dóminum flagellávit, sed eórum furóri satisfácere volens: ut vel sic jam mitéscerent, et desínerent velle occídere, cum flagellátum vidérent. Fecit et hoc. At ubi perseveravérunt, nostis illum lavísse manus, et dixísse, quod ipse non fecísset, mundum se esse a morte illíus. Fecit tamen. Sed si reus, quia fecit vel invítus: illi innocéntes, qui coëgérunt ut fáceret? Nullo modo. Sed ille dixit in eum senténtiam, et jussit eum crucifígi, et quasi ipse occídit: et vos, o Judǽi, occidístis. Unde occidístis? Gládio linguæ: acuístis enim linguas vestras. Et quando percussístis, nisi quando clamástis: Crucifíge, crucifíge?
lectio6.eng: They whetted their tongue like a sword. The Jews cannot say: We did not murder Christ, albeit they gave Him over to Pilate His judge, that they themselves might seem free of His death. For when Pilate said unto them, Take ye Him: and kill Him, they answered, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death. They could throw the blame of their sin upon a human judge: but did they deceive God, the Great Judge? In that which Pilate did, he was their accomplice, but in comparison with them, he had far the lesser sin. (John xix. 11.) Pilate strove as far as he could, to deliver Him out of their hands; for the which reason also he scourged Him, (John xix. 1,) and brought Him forth to them. He scourged not the Lord for cruelty's sake, but in the hope that; he might so slake their wild thirst for blood: that, perchance, even they might be touched with compassion, and cease to lust for His death, when they saw What He was after the flagellation. Even this effort he made! But when Pilate saw that he could not prevail, but that rather a tumult was made, (Matth. xxvii. 24,) ye know how that he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying: I am innocent of the blood of this Just Person. And yet he delivered Him to be crucified! But if he were guilty who did it against his will, were they innocent; who goaded him on to it? No. Pilate gave sentence against Him. and commanded Him to be crucified. But ye, O ye Jews, ye also are His murderers! Wherewith? With your tongue, whetted like a sword. And when? But when ye cried, Crucify Him! Crucify Him! (Mark xv.13-14)

responsory6.lat:
R. Animam meam diléctam trádidi in manus iniquórum, et facta est mihi heréditas mea sicut leo in silva: dedit contra me voces adversárius, dicens: Congregámini, et properáte ad devorándum illum: posuérunt me in desérto solitúdinis, et luxit super me omnis terra:
* Quia non est invéntus qui me agnósceret, et fáceret bene.
V. Insurrexérunt in me viri absque misericórdia, et non pepercérunt ánimæ meæ.
R. Quia non est invéntus qui me agnósceret, et fáceret bene.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Animam meam diléctam trádidi in manus iniquórum, et facta est mihi heréditas mea sicut leo in silva: dedit contra me voces adversárius, dicens: Congregámini, et properáte ad devorándum illum: posuérunt me in desérto solitúdinis, et luxit super me omnis terra: * Quia non est invéntus qui me agnósceret, et fáceret bene.
responsory6.eng:
R. I have given the dearly-beloved of My soul into the hand of her enemies and Mine heritage is become unto Me as a lion in the forest; the enemy crieth out against Me, saying: Assemble yourselves together, hasten to devour Him: they have made My portion a desolate wilderness, and the whole land mourneth unto Me:
* Because there is none found that will know Me, nor do well.
V. There be risen up against me such as breathe out cruelty, and they have not spared my soul.
R. Because there is none found that will know Me, nor do well.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. I have given the dearly-beloved of My soul into the hand of her enemies, and Mine heritage is become unto Me as a lion in the forest: the enemy crieth out against Me, saying: Assemble yourselves together, hasten to devour Him: they have made My portion a desolate wilderness, and the whole land mourneth unto me: * Because there is none found that will know Me, nor do well.

lectio7.lat:
De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Hebrǽos
11 Festinémus íngredi in illam réquiem: ut ne in idípsum quis íncidat incredulitátis exémplum.
12 Vivus est enim sermo Dei, et éfficax et penetrabílior omni gládio ancípiti: et pertíngens usque ad divisiónem ánimæ ac spíritus, compágum quoque ac medullárum, et discrétor cogitatiónum et intentiónum cordis.
13 Et non est ulla creatúra invisíbilis in conspéctu ejus: ómnia autem nuda et apérta sunt óculis ejus, ad quem nobis sermo.
14 Habéntes ergo Pontíficem magnum, qui penetrávit cælos, Jesum Fílium Dei: teneámus confessiónem.
15 Non enim habémus Pontíficem, qui non possit cómpati infirmitátibus nostris: tentátum autem per ómnia pro similitúdine absque peccáto.
lectio7.eng:
From the letter of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews
11 Let us hasten therefore to enter into that rest; lest any man fall into the same example of unbelief.
12 For the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two edged sword; and reaching unto the division of the soul and the spirit, of the joints also and the marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
13 Neither is there any creature invisible in his sight: but all things are naked and open to his eyes, to whom our speech is.
14 Having therefore a great high priest that hath passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God: let us hold fast our confession.
15 For we have not a high priest, who can not have compassion on our infirmities: but one tempted in all things like as we are, without sin.

responsory7.lat:
R. Tradidérunt me in manus impiórum, et inter iníquos projecérunt me, et non pepercérunt ánimæ meæ: congregáti sunt advérsum me fortes:
* Et sicut gigántes stetérunt contra me.
V. Aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.
R. Et sicut gigántes stetérunt contra me.
responsory7.eng:
R. They have turned me over into the hands of the wicked: they also have numbered me with the transgressors, neither have they spared my life: the mighty are gathered together against me;
* And stand up against me like giants.
V. Strangers are risen up against me, and oppressors seek after my soul.
R. And stand up against me like giants.

lectio8.lat:
16 Adeámus ergo cum fidúcia ad thronum grátiæ: ut misericórdiam consequámur, et grátiam inveniámus in auxílio opportúno.
1 Omnis namque Póntifex ex homínibus assúmptus, pro homínibus constitúitur in iis, quæ sunt ad Deum, ut ófferat dona, et sacrifícia pro peccátis:
2 qui condolére possit iis, qui ignórant et errant: quóniam et ipse circúmdatus est infirmitáte:
3 et proptérea debet quemádmodum pro pópulo, ita étiam pro semetípso offérre pro peccátis.
lectio8.eng:
16 Let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace: that we may obtain mercy, and find grace in seasonable aid.
1 For every high priest taken from among men, is ordained for men in the things that appertain to God, that he may offer up gifts and sacrifices for sins:
2 Who can have compassion on them that are ignorant and that err: because he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
3 And therefore he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

responsory8.lat:
R. Jesum trádidit ímpius summis princípibus sacerdótum, et senióribus pópuli:
* Petrus autem sequebátur eum a longe, ut vidéret finem.
V. Adduxérunt autem eum ad Cáipham príncipem sacerdótum, ubi scribæ et pharisǽi convénerant.
R. Petrus autem sequebátur eum a longe, ut vidéret finem.
responsory8.eng:
R. That wicked one betrayed Jesus to the chief-priests and elders of the people
* But Peter followed Him afar off, to see the end.
V. And they led Him away to Caiaphas the High Priest, where the Scribes and Pharisees were assembled.
R. But Peter followed Him afar off, to see the end.

lectio9.lat:
4 Nec quisquam sumit sibi honórem, sed qui vocátur a Deo, tamquam Aaron.
5 Sic et Christus non semetípsum clarificávit ut Póntifex fíeret, sed qui locútus est ad eum: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
6 Quemádmodum et in álio loco dicit: Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum, secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
7 Qui in diébus carnis suæ preces, supplicationésque ad eum, qui possit illum salvum fácere a morte, cum clamóre válido et lácrimis ófferens, exaudítus est pro sua reveréntia.
8 Et quidem cum esset Fílius Dei, dídicit ex iis, quæ passus est, obediéntiam:
9 et consummátus, factus est ómnibus obtemperántibus sibi causa salútis ætérnæ,
10 appellátus a Deo Póntifex juxta órdinem Melchísedech.
lectio9.eng:
4 Neither doth any man take the honour to himself, but he that is called by God, as Aaron was.
5 So Christ also did not glorify himself, that he might be made a high priest: but he that said unto him: Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
6 As he saith also in another place: Thou art a priest for ever, according to the order of Melchisedech.
7 Who in the days of his flesh, with a strong cry and tears, offering up prayers and supplications to him that was able to save him from death, was heard for his reverence.
8 And whereas indeed he was the Son of God, he learned obedience by the things which he suffered:
9 And being consummated, he became, to all that obey him, the cause of eternal salvation.
10 Called by God a high priest according to the order of Melchisedech.

responsory9.lat:
R. Caligavérunt óculi mei a fletu meo: quia elongátus est a me, qui consolabátur me: Vidéte omnes pópuli,
* Si est dolor símilis sicut dolor meus.
V. O vos omnes, qui transítis per viam, atténdite et vidéte.
R. Si est dolor símilis sicut dolor meus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Caligavérunt óculi mei a fletu meo: quia elongátus est a me, qui consolabátur me: Vidéte omnes pópuli, * Si est dolor símilis sicut dolor meus.
responsory9.eng:
R. Mine eyes do fail with tears, because the Comforter that should relieve me is far from me. Behold, O all ye nations
* If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.
V. O all ye that pass by, behold, and see
R. If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. Mine eyes do fail with tears, because the Comforter that should relieve me is far from me. Behold, O all ye nations, * If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.

oratio_matutinum.lat: Réspice, quǽsumus, Dómine, super hanc famíliam tuam, pro qua Dóminus noster Jesus Christus non dubitávit mánibus tradi nocéntium, et crucis subíre torméntum:
oratio_matutinum.eng: O Lord, we beseech Thee, behold this Thy family, for which our Lord Jesus Christ was contented to be betrayed, and given up into the hands of wicked men, and to suffer death upon the Cross.

ant_laudes.lat:
Próprio * Fílio suo non pepércit Deus, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum.
Anxiátus est super me * spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.
Ait latro ad latrónem: * Nos quidem digna factis recípimus, hic autem quid fecit? Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
Cum conturbáta fúerit * ánima mea, Dómine, misericórdiæ memor eris.
Meménto mei, * Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
ant_laudes.eng:
God spared not His Own Son * but delivered Him up for us all.
My spirit is overwhelmed within me; * my heart within me is troubled.
One thief said unto the other: * We indeed receive the due reward of our deeds, but what hath this man done? Lord, remember me, when thou comest into thy kingdom.
Lord, when my soul is troubled, * thou wilt remember mercy.
Lord, remember me * when thou comest into thy kingdom.

versum_2.lat:
V. Collocávit me in obscúris.
R. Sicut mórtuos sǽculi.
versum_2.eng:
V. He hath set me in dark places.
R. As they that be dead of old.

ant_2.lat: Posuérunt * super caput ejus causam ipsíus scriptam: Jesus Nazarénus, Rex Judæórum.
ant_2.eng: They set up over his head his accusation written: * Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.

versum_3.lat:
V. Collocávit me in obscúris.
R. Sicut mórtuos sǽculi.
versum_3.eng:
V. He hath set me in dark places.
R. As they that be dead of old.

ant_3.lat: Cum accepísset acétum, * dixit: Consummátum est: et inclináto cápite, emísit spíritum.
ant_3.eng: When He had received the vinegar, * he said: It is finished! and he bowed his Head, and gave up the Ghost.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum, advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: The kings of the earth set themselves, * and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Divisérunt sibi * vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: They part my garments among them, * and cast lots upon my vesture.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Insurrexérunt in me * testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: False witnesses are risen up against me, * and iniquity hath belied itself.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Vim faciébant, * qui quærébant ánimam meam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: They that sought after my life * have used violence again me.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Confundántur * et revereántur, qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Let them be ashamed and confounded * together that seek after my soul, to destroy it.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Aliéni * insurrexérunt in me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: Strangers are risen up against me, * and oppressors seek after my soul.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Ab insurgéntibus in me * líbera me, Dómine, quia occupavérunt ánimam meam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: O Lord, defend me from them that rise up against me, * for they lie in wait for my life.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Longe fecísti * notos meos a me: tráditus sum, et non egrediébar.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; * I am shut up, and cannot come forth.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Captábunt * in ánimam justi, et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: They gather themselves together * against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.

verses.lat: Quare fremuérunt gentes: et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
verses.eng: Why have the Gentiles raged, and the people devised vain things?

verses.lat: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
verses.eng: The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, against the Lord and against his Christ.

verses.lat: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: et proiciámus a nobis jugum ipsórum.
verses.eng: Let us break their bonds asunder: and let us cast away their yoke from us.

verses.lat: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
verses.eng: He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: and the Lord shall deride them.

verses.lat: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
verses.eng: Then shall he speak to them in his anger, and trouble them in his rage.

verses.lat: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
verses.eng: But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, preaching his commandment.

verses.lat: Dóminus dixit ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
verses.eng: The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

verses.lat: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
verses.eng: Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

verses.lat: Reges eos in virga férrea, et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
verses.eng: Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

verses.lat: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: erudímini, qui judicátis terram.
verses.eng: And now, O ye kings, understand: receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

verses.lat: Servíte Dómino in timóre: et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
verses.eng: Serve ye the Lord with fear: and rejoice unto him with trembling.

verses.lat: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, et pereátis de via justa.
verses.eng: Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, and you perish from the just way.

verses.lat: Cum exárserit in brevi ira ejus: beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
verses.eng: When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, blessed are all they that trust in him.

verses.lat: Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
verses.eng: O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.

verses.lat: Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
verses.eng: O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.

verses.lat: Tu autem in sancto hábitas, laus Israël.
verses.eng: But thou dwellest in the holy place, the praise of Israel.

verses.lat: In te speravérunt patres nostri: speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
verses.eng: In thee have our fathers hoped: they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.

verses.lat: Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
verses.eng: They cried to thee, and they were saved: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.

verses.lat: Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: oppróbrium hóminum, et abjéctio plebis.
verses.eng: But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.

verses.lat: Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
verses.eng: All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.

verses.lat: Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
verses.eng: He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.

verses.lat: Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te projéctus sum ex útero:
verses.eng: For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.

verses.lat: De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, ne discésseris a me:
verses.eng: From my mother’s womb thou art my God, depart not from me.

verses.lat: Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: quóniam non est qui ádjuvet.
verses.eng: For tribulation is very near: for there is none to help me.
