verses.lat: Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
verses.eng: Many calves have surrounded me: fat bulls have besieged me.

verses.lat: Aperuérunt super me os suum, sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
verses.eng: They have opened their mouths against me, as a lion ravening and roaring.

verses.lat: Sicut aqua effúsus sum: et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: I am poured out like water; and all my bones are scattered.

verses.lat: Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
verses.eng: My heart is become like wax melting in the midst of my bowels.

verses.lat: Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis: et in púlverem mortis deduxísti me.
verses.eng: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.

verses.lat: Quóniam circumdedérunt me canes multi: concílium malignántium obsédit me.
verses.eng: For many dogs have encompassed me: the council of the malignant hath besieged me.

verses.lat: Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: They have dug my hands and feet. They have numbered all my bones.

verses.lat: Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
verses.eng: And they have looked and stared upon me. They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
verses.eng: But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; look towards my defence.

verses.lat: Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam: et de manu canis únicam meam:
verses.eng: Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: my only one from the hand of the dog.

verses.lat: Salva me ex ore leónis: et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
verses.eng: Save me from the lion’s mouth; and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.

verses.lat: Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
verses.eng: I will declare thy name to my brethren: in the midst of the church will I praise thee.

verses.lat: Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: univérsum semen Jacob, glorificáte eum.
verses.eng: Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.

verses.lat: Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
verses.eng: Let all the seed of Israel fear him: because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.

verses.lat: Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
verses.eng: Neither hath he turned away his face from me: and when I cried to him he heard me.

verses.lat: Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
verses.eng: With thee is my praise in a great church: I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.

verses.lat: Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: their hearts shall live for ever and ever.

verses.lat: Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum univérsi fines terræ:
verses.eng: All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:

verses.lat: Et adorábunt in conspéctu ejus univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
verses.eng: And all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight.

verses.lat: Quóniam Dómini est regnum: et ipse dominábitur géntium.
verses.eng: For the kingdom is the Lord’s; and he shall have dominion over the nations.

verses.lat: Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: in conspéctu ejus cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
verses.eng: All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.

verses.lat: Et ánima mea illi vivet: et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
verses.eng: And to him my soul shall live: and my seed shall serve him.

verses.lat: Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
verses.eng: There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.

verses.lat: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, quem timébo?
verses.eng: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?

verses.lat: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, a quo trepidábo?
verses.eng: The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.lat: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, ut edant carnes meas:
verses.eng: Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh.

verses.lat: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
verses.eng: My enemies that trouble me, have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

verses.lat: Si consístant advérsum me castra, non timébit cor meum.
verses.eng: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear.

verses.lat: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, in hoc ego sperábo.
verses.eng: If a battle should rise up against me, in this will I be confident.

verses.lat: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

verses.lat: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, et vísitem templum ejus.
verses.eng: That I may see the delight of the Lord, and may visit his temple.

verses.lat: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
verses.eng: For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

verses.lat: In petra exaltávit me: et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
verses.eng: He hath exalted me upon a rock: and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

verses.lat: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
verses.eng: I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: miserére mei, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: have mercy on me and hear me.

verses.lat: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
verses.eng: My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

verses.lat: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
verses.eng: Turn not away thy face from me; decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus esto: ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
verses.eng: Be thou my helper, forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

verses.lat: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
verses.eng: For my father and my mother have left me: but the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.lat: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
verses.eng: Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

verses.lat: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
verses.eng: Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

verses.lat: Credo vidére bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
verses.eng: Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

verses.lat: Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, neque in ira tua corrípias me.
verses.eng: Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; nor chastise me in thy wrath.

verses.lat: Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
verses.eng: For thy arrows are fastened in me: and thy hand hath been strong upon me.

verses.lat: Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
verses.eng: There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.

verses.lat: Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
verses.eng: For my iniquities are gone over my head: and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.

verses.lat: Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
verses.eng: My sores are putrified and corrupted, because of my foolishness.

verses.lat: Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
verses.eng: I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: I walked sorrowful all the day long.

verses.lat: Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: et non est sánitas in carne mea.
verses.eng: For my loins are filled with illusions; and there is no health in my flesh.

verses.lat: Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
verses.eng: I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: I roared with the groaning of my heart.

verses.lat: Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.
verses.eng: Lord, all my desire is before thee, and my groaning is not hidden from thee.

verses.lat: Cor meum conturbátum est, derelíquit me virtus mea: et lumen oculórum meórum, et ipsum non est mecum.
verses.eng: My heart is troubled, my strength hath left me, and the light of my eyes itself is not with me.

verses.lat: Amíci mei, et próximi mei advérsum me appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt.
verses.eng: My friends and my neighbours have drawn near, and stood against me.

verses.lat: Et qui juxta me erant, de longe stetérunt: et vim faciébant qui quærébant ánimam meam.
verses.eng: And they that were near me stood afar off: and they that sought my soul used violence.

verses.lat: Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: et dolos tota die meditabántur.
verses.eng: And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, and studied deceits all the day long.

verses.lat: Ego autem tamquam surdus non audiébam: et sicut mutus non apériens os suum.
verses.eng: But I, as a deaf man, heard not: and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.

verses.lat: Et factus sum sicut homo non áudiens: et non habens in ore suo redargutiónes.
verses.eng: And I became as a man that heareth not: and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.

verses.lat: Quóniam in te, Dómine, sperávi: tu exáudies me, Dómine, Deus meus.
verses.eng: For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.

verses.lat: Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei: et dum commovéntur pedes mei, super me magna locúti sunt.
verses.eng: For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.

verses.lat: Quóniam ego in flagélla parátus sum: et dolor meus in conspéctu meo semper.
verses.eng: For I am ready for scourges: and my sorrow is continually before me.

verses.lat: Quóniam iniquitátem meam annuntiábo: et cogitábo pro peccáto meo.
verses.eng: For I will declare my iniquity: and I will think for my sin.

verses.lat: Inimíci autem mei vivunt, et confirmáti sunt super me: et multiplicáti sunt qui odérunt me iníque.
verses.eng: But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.

verses.lat: Qui retríbuunt mala pro bonis, detrahébant mihi: quóniam sequébar bonitátem.
verses.eng: They that render evil for good, have detracted me, because I followed goodness.

verses.lat: Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: ne discésseris a me.
verses.eng: Forsake me not, O Lord my God: do not thou depart from me.

verses.lat: Inténde in adjutórium meum, Dómine, Deus, salútis meæ.
verses.eng: Attend unto my help, O Lord, the God of my salvation.

verses.lat: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, and he was attentive to me.

verses.lat: Et exaudívit preces meas: et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: And he heard my prayers, and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: Et státuit super petram pedes meos: et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: And he set my feet upon a rock, and directed my steps.

verses.lat: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: And he put a new canticle into my mouth, a song to our God.

verses.lat: Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: Many shall see, and shall fear: and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

verses.lat: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi et locútus sum: multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: I have declared and I have spoken they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; but thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
verses.eng: Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: then said I, Behold I come.

verses.lat: In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: I have declared thy justice in a great church, lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

verses.lat: Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: I have not hid thy justice within my heart: I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

verses.lat: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam a concílio multo.
verses.eng: I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth from a great council.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: For evils without number have surrounded me; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul to take it away.

verses.lat: Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be turned backward and be ashamed that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: Let them immediately bear their confusion, that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: But I am a beggar and poor: the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: Thou art my helper and my protector: O my God, be not slack.

verses.lat: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: et in virtúte tua júdica me.
verses.eng: Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.

verses.lat: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
verses.eng: O God, hear my prayer: give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
verses.eng: For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: and they have not set God before their eyes.

verses.lat: Ecce enim, Deus ádjuvat me: et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: For behold God is my helper: and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: Avérte mala inimícis meis: et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
verses.eng: Turn back the evils upon my enemies; and cut them off in thy truth.

verses.lat: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
verses.eng: I will freely sacrifice to thee, and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

verses.lat: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
verses.eng: For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

verses.lat: Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus: et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
verses.eng: Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; and defend me from them that rise up against me.

verses.lat: Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem: et de viris sánguinum salva me.
verses.eng: Deliver me from them that work iniquity, and save me from bloody men.

verses.lat: Quia ecce cepérunt ánimam meam: irruérunt in me fortes.
verses.eng: For behold they have caught my soul: the mighty have rushed in upon me:

verses.lat: Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine: sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi.
verses.eng: Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.

verses.lat: Exsúrge in occúrsum meum, et vide: et tu, Dómine, Deus virtútum, Deus Israël,
verses.eng: Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel.

verses.lat: Inténde ad visitándas omnes gentes: non misereáris ómnibus, qui operántur iniquitátem.
verses.eng: Attend to visit all the nations: have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.

verses.lat: Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, et circuíbunt civitátem.
verses.eng: They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: and shall go round about the city.

verses.lat: Ecce, loquéntur in ore suo, et gládius in lábiis eórum: quóniam quis audívit?
verses.eng: Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: for who, say they, hath heard us?

verses.lat: Et tu, Dómine, deridébis eos: ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes.
verses.eng: But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.

verses.lat: Fortitúdinem meam ad te custódiam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: Deus meus, misericórdia ejus prævéniet me.
verses.eng: I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector: my God, his mercy shall prevent me.

verses.lat: Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos, ne occídas eos: nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei.
verses.eng: God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, lest at any time my people forget.

verses.lat: Dispérge illos in virtúte tua: et depóne eos, protéctor meus, Dómine:
verses.eng: And scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:

verses.lat: Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum: et comprehendántur in supérbia sua.
verses.eng: For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: and let them be taken in their pride.

verses.lat: Et de exsecratióne et mendácio annuntiabúntur in consummatióne: in ira consummatiónis, et non erunt.
verses.eng: And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of, when they are consumed: when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more.

verses.lat: Et scient quia Deus dominábitur Jacob: et fínium terræ.
verses.eng: And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, and all the ends of the earth.

verses.lat: Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, et circuíbunt civitátem.
verses.eng: They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: and shall go round about the city.

verses.lat: Ipsi dispergéntur ad manducándum: si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt.
verses.eng: They shall be scattered abroad to eat, and shall murmur if they be not filled.

verses.lat: Ego autem cantábo fortitúdinem tuam: et exsultábo mane misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: But I will sing thy strength: and will extol thy mercy in the morning.

verses.lat: Quia factus es suscéptor meus, et refúgium meum, in die tribulatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: For thou art become my support, and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: Deus meus, misericórdia mea.
verses.eng: Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: my God my mercy.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
verses.eng: Lord, the God of my salvation: I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.

verses.lat: Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
verses.eng: Let my prayer come in before thee: incline thy ear to my petition.

verses.lat: Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
verses.eng: For my soul is filled with evils: and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

verses.lat: Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
verses.eng: I am counted among them that go down to the pit: I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

verses.lat: Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
verses.eng: Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: and they are cast off from thy hand.

verses.lat: Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
verses.eng: They have laid me in the lower pit: in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

verses.lat: Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
verses.eng: Thy wrath is strong over me: and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

verses.lat: Longe fecísti notos meos a me: posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: they have set me an abomination to themselves.

verses.lat: Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
verses.eng: I was delivered up, and came not forth: my eyes languished through poverty.

verses.lat: Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: expándi ad te manus meas.
verses.eng: All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: I stretched out my hands to thee.

verses.lat: Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
verses.eng: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

verses.lat: Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
verses.eng: Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: and thy truth in destruction?

verses.lat: Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, et justítia tua in terra obliviónis?
verses.eng: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

verses.lat: Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
verses.eng: But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

verses.lat: Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: avértis fáciem tuam a me?
verses.eng: Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: why turnest thou away thy face from me?

verses.lat: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a juventúte mea: exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
verses.eng: I am poor, and in labours from my youth: and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

verses.lat: In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
verses.eng: Thy wrath hath come upon me: and thy terrors have troubled me.

verses.lat: Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: circumdedérunt me simul.
verses.eng: They have come round about me like water all the day: they have compassed me about together.

verses.lat: Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: et notos meos a miséria.
verses.eng: Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: and my acquaintance, because of misery.

verses.lat: Deus ultiónum Dóminus: Deus ultiónum líbere egit.
verses.eng: The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: the God of revenge hath acted freely.

verses.lat: Exaltáre, qui júdicas terram: redde retributiónem supérbis.
verses.eng: Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: render a reward to the proud.

verses.lat: Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:
verses.eng: How long shall sinners, O Lord: how long shall sinners glory?

verses.lat: Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: loquéntur omnes, qui operántur injustítiam?
verses.eng: Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: shall all speak who work injustice?

verses.lat: Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.
verses.eng: Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: and they have afflicted thy inheritance.

verses.lat: Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: et pupíllos occidérunt.
verses.eng: They have slain the widow and the stranger: and they have murdered the fatherless.

verses.lat: Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, nec intélleget Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: And they have said: The Lord shall not see: neither shall the God of Jacob understand.

verses.lat: Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: et stulti, aliquándo sápite.
verses.eng: Understand, ye senseless among the people: and, you fools, be wise at last.

verses.lat: Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?
verses.eng: He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?

verses.lat: Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?
verses.eng: He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: he that teacheth man knowledge?

verses.lat: Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, quóniam vanæ sunt.
verses.eng: The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, that they are vain.

verses.lat: Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: et de lege tua docúeris eum,
verses.eng: Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: and shalt teach him out of thy law.

verses.lat: Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.
verses.eng: That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: till a pit be dug for the wicked.

verses.lat: Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.
verses.eng: For the Lord will not cast off his people: neither will he forsake his own inheritance.

verses.lat: Quoadúsque justítia convertátur in judícium: et qui juxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.
verses.eng: Until justice be turned into judgment: and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.

verses.lat: Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?
verses.eng: Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?

verses.lat: Nisi quia Dóminus adjúvit me: paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.
verses.eng: Unless the Lord had been my helper, my soul had almost dwelt in hell.

verses.lat: Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: misericórdia tua, Dómine, adjuvábat me.
verses.eng: If I said: My foot is moved: thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me.

verses.lat: Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

verses.lat: Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: qui fingis labórem in præcépto?
verses.eng: Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee, who framest labour in commandment?

verses.lat: Captábunt in ánimam justi: et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
verses.eng: They will hunt after the soul of the just, and will condemn innocent blood.

verses.lat: Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: et Deus meus in adjutórium spei meæ.
verses.eng: But the Lord is my refuge: and my God the help of my hope.

verses.lat: Et reddet illis iniquitátem ipsórum: et in malítia eórum dispérdet eos: dispérdet illos Dóminus, Deus noster.
verses.eng: And he will render them their iniquity: and in their malice he will destroy them: the Lord our God will destroy them.

ant_matutinum.lat:
In pace * in idípsum, dórmiam et requiéscam.
Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Caro mea * requiéscet in spe.
Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
Dómine, * abstraxísti ab ínferis ánimam meam.
Deus ádjuvat me, * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
In pace * factus est locus ejus, et in Sion habitátio ejus.
Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
ant_matutinum.eng:
I will both lay me down in peace, * and sleep.
He shall abide in thy tabernacle: * he shall dwell in thy holy hill.
My flesh * shall rest in hope.
Be ye lift up, * ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.
I believe that I shall yet see * the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.
O Lord, Thou hast brought up * my soul from the grave.
God is my helper, * and the Lord upholdeth my soul.
His place is in peace * and His dwelling-place in Zion.
I am as a man that hath no strength, * lying nerveless among the dead.

nocturn_1_versum.lat:
V. In pace in idípsum.
R. Dórmiam et requiéscam.
nocturn_1_versum.eng:
V. I will both lay me down in peace.
R. And sleep.

nocturn_2_versum.lat:
V. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei.
R. Et resúscita me, et retríbuam eis.
nocturn_2_versum.eng:
V. But Thou, O Lord, be merciful unto me.
R. And raise me up; and I will requite them.

nocturn_3_versum.lat:
V. In pace factus est locus ejus.
R. Et in Sion habitátio ejus.
nocturn_3_versum.eng:
V. His place is in peace.
R. And His dwelling-place in Zion.

lectio1.lat:
De Lamentatióne Jeremíæ Prophétæ
22 Heth. Misericórdiæ Dómini quia non sumus consúmpti: quia non defecérunt miseratiónes ejus.
23 Heth. Novi dilúculo, multa est fides tua.
24 Heth. Pars mea Dóminus, dixit ánima mea: proptérea exspectábo eum.
25 Teth. Bonus est Dóminus sperántibus in eum, ánimæ quærénti illum.
26 Teth. Bonum est præstolári cum siléntio salutáre Dei.
27 Teth. Bonum est viro cum portáverit jugum ab adulescéntia sua.
28 Jod. Sedébit solitárius, et tacébit: quia levávit super se.
29 Jod. Ponet in púlvere os suum, si forte sit spes.
30 Jod. Dabit percutiénti se maxíllam, saturábitur oppróbriis.
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio1.eng:
Lesson from the book of Lamentations
22 Heth. The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed.
23 Heth. They are new every morning, great is thy faithfulness.
24 Heth. The Lord is my portion, said my soul: therefore will I wait for him.
25 Teth. The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him.
26 Teth. It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of God.
27 Teth. It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke from his youth.
28 Jod. He shall sit solitary, and hold his peace: because he hath taken it up upon himself.
29 Jod. He shall put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.
30 Jod. He shall give his cheek to him that striketh him, he shall be filled with reproaches.
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory1.lat:
R. Sicut ovis ad occisiónem ductus est, et dum male tractarétur, non apéruit os suum: tráditus est ad mortem,
* Ut vivificáret pópulum suum.
V. Trádidit in mortem ánimam suam, et inter scelerátos reputátus est.
R. Ut vivificáret pópulum suum.
responsory1.eng:
R. He hath been brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and while he was evil entreated he opened not his mouth: he was delivered up to death
* That he might quicken his people.
V. He hath poured out his soul unto death, and he was numbered with the transgressors.
R. That he might quicken his people.

lectio2.lat:
1 Aleph. Quómodo obscurátum est aurum, mutátus est color óptimus, dispérsi sunt lápides sanctuárii in cápite ómnium plateárum?
2 Beth. Fílii Sion íncliti, et amícti auro primo: quómodo reputáti sunt in vasa téstea, opus mánuum fíguli?
3 Ghimel. Sed et lámiæ nudavérunt mammam, lactavérunt cátulos suos: fília pópuli mei crudélis, quasi strúthio in desérto.
4 Daleth. Adhǽsit lingua lacténtis ad palátum ejus in siti: párvuli petiérunt panem, et non erat qui frángeret eis.
5 He. Qui vescebántur voluptuóse, interiérunt in viis: qui nutriebántur in cróceis, amplexáti sunt stércora.
6 Vau. Et major effécta est iníquitas fíliæ pópuli mei peccáto Sodomórum, quæ subvérsa est in moménto, et non cepérunt in ea manus.
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio2.eng:
1 Aleph. How is the gold become dim, the finest colour is changed, the stones of the sanctuary are scattered in the top of every street?
2 Beth. The noble sons of Sion, and they that were clothed with the best gold: how are they esteemed as earthen vessels, the work of the potter's hands?
3 Ghimel. Even the sea monsters have drawn out the breast, they have given suck to their young: the daughter of my people is cruel, like the ostrich in the desert.
4 Daleth. The tongue of the sucking child hath stuck to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the little ones have asked for bread, and there was none to break it unto them.
5 He. They that were fed delicately have died in the streets; they that were brought up in scarlet have embraced the dung.
6 Vau. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people is made greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and hands took nothing in her.
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory2.lat:
R. Jerúsalem, surge, et éxue te véstibus jucunditátis: indúere cínere et cilício,
* Quia in te occísus est Salvátor Israël.
V. Deduc quasi torréntem lácrimas per diem et noctem, et non táceat pupílla óculi tui.
R. Quia in te occísus est Salvátor Israël.
responsory2.eng:
R. Arise, O Jerusalem, and put off thy garments of rejoicing: cover thee with sackcloth and ashes
* For the Saviour of Israel hath been slain in the midst of thee.
V. Let thy tears run down like a river day and night, and let not the apple of thine eye cease.
R. For the Saviour of Israel hath been slain in the midst of thee.

lectio3.lat:
Incipit Orátio Jeremíæ Prophétæ
1 Recordáre, Dómine, quid accíderit nobis: intuére, et réspice oppróbrium nostrum.
2 Heréditas nostra versa est ad aliénos: domus nostræ ad extráneos.
3 Pupílli facti sumus absque patre, matres nostræ quasi víduæ.
4 Aquam nostram pecúnia bíbimus: ligna nostra prétio comparávimus.
5 Cervícibus nostris minabámur, lassis non dabátur réquies.
6 Ægýpto dédimus manum, et Assýriis, ut saturarémur pane.
7 Patres nostri peccavérunt, et non sunt: et nos iniquitátes eórum portávimus.
8 Servi domináti sunt nostri: non fuit qui redímeret de manu eórum.
9 In animábus nostris afferebámus panem nobis, a fácie gládii in desérto.
10 Pellis nostra quasi clíbanus exústa est a fácie tempestátum famis.
11 Mulíeres in Sion humiliavérunt, et vírgines in civitátibus Juda.
Jerúsalem, Jerúsalem, convértere ad Dóminum Deum tuum.
lectio3.eng:
1 Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider and behold our reproach.
2 Our inheritance is turned to aliens: our houses to strangers.
3 We are become orphans without a father: our mothers are as widows.
4 We have drunk our water for money: we have bought our wood.
5 We were dragged by the necks, we were weary and no rest was given us.
6 We have given our hand to Egypt, and to the Assyrians, that we might be satisfied with bread.
7 Our fathers have sinned, and are not: and we have borne their iniquities.
8 Servants have ruled over us: there was none to redeem us out of their hand.
9 We fetched our bread at the peril of our lives, because of the sword in the desert.
10 Our skin was burnt as an oven, by reason of the violence of the famine.
11 They oppressed the women in Sion, and the virgins in the cities of Juda.
Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Return unto the Lord thy God.

responsory3.lat:
R. Plange quasi virgo, plebs mea: ululáte, pastóres, in cínere et cilício:
* Quia venit dies Dómini magna, et amára valde.
V. Accíngite vos, sacerdótes, et plángite, minístri altáris, aspérgite vos cínere.
R. Quia venit dies Dómini magna, et amára valde.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Plange quasi virgo, plebs mea: ululáte, pastóres, in cínere et cilício: * Quia venit dies Dómini magna, et amára valde.
responsory3.eng:
R. O my people! lament, like a virgin girded with sack-cloth for the husband of her youth, howl, ye shepherds, in sack-cloth and ashes
* For the day of the Lord is at hand, and it is great and very terrible.
V. Gird yourselves, ye Priests, and howl, ye ministers of the altar: cast up ashes upon you.
R. For the day of the Lord is at hand, and it is great and very terrible.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. O my people! lament, like a virgin, girded with sack-cloth for the husband of her youth, howl, ye shepherds, in sack-cloth and ashes * For the day of the Lord is at hand, and it is great and very terrible.

lectio4.lat:
Ex Tractátu sancti Augustíni Epíscopi super Psalmos
Accédet homo ad cor altum, et exaltábitur Deus. Illi dixérunt: Quis nos vidébit? Defecérunt scrutántes scrutatiónes, consília mala. Accéssit homo ad ipsa consília, passus est se tenéri ut homo. Non enim tenerétur nisi homo, aut viderétur nisi homo, aut cæderétur nisi homo, aut crucifigerétur, aut morerétur nisi homo. Accéssit ergo homo ad illas omnes passiónes, quæ in illo nihil valérent, nisi esset homo. Sed si ille non esset homo, non liberarétur homo. Accéssit homo ad cor altum, id est, cor secrétum, obíciens aspéctibus humánis hóminem, servans intus Deum: celans formam Dei, in qua æquális est Patri, et ófferens formam servi, qua minor est Patre.
lectio4.eng:
From the Treatise of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo,) Upon the Psalms
We shall attain to thoughts that are very deep: but God shall still be exalted. The enemies of our Lord had communed of laying snares privily; they had said, Who shall see them? They had searched out iniquities; they had accomplished a diligent search. And Man attained even unto (the realization of) their counsels, for the Lord, as Man, suffered Himself to be taken. For He had not been taken at all, unless He had been a Man, or seen, unless He had been a Man, or smitten, unless He had been a Man, or crucified, unless He had been a Man, or have died, unless He had been a Man. Man therefore, He attained unto all those sufferings, which had had nothing in Him, unless He had been a Man. But if He had not been Man, man had not been redeemed. And the Lord as Man attained to thoughts that were very deep, yea, secret; showing the Manhood to the eyes of men, and keeping the Godhead within Him; veiling the form of God, as touching Which, He is Equal to the Father, and manifesting the form of a servant, as touching which, He is inferior to the Father.

responsory4.lat:
R. Recéssit pastor noster, fons aquæ vivæ, ad cujus tránsitum sol obscurátus est:
* Nam et ille captus est, qui captívum tenébat primum hóminem: hódie portas mortis et seras páriter Salvátor noster disrúpit.
V. Destrúxit quidem claustra inférni, et subvértit poténtias diáboli.
R. Nam et ille captus est, qui captívum tenébat primum hóminem: hódie portas mortis et seras páriter Salvátor noster disrúpit.
responsory4.eng:
R. Our Shepherd, even the Fountain of living waters, is gone from us; He passed away, and the sun was darkened.
* For now hath our Saviour bound him captive, which bound the first man captive; this day hath He burst the gates and bars of death.
V. The bands of hell He hath utterly abolished, and hath done away the power of the devil.
R. For now hath our Saviour bound him captive, which bound the first man captive; this day hath He burst the gates and bars of death.

lectio5.lat: Quo perduxérunt illas scrutatiónes suas, quas perscrutántes defecérunt, ut étiam mórtuo Dómino et sepúlto, custódes pónerent ad sepúlcrum? Dixérunt enim Piláto: Sedúctor ille: hoc appellabátur nómine Dóminus Jesus Christus, ad solátium servórum suórum, quando dicúntur seductóres: ergo illi Piláto: Sedúctor ille, ínquiunt, dixit adhuc vivens: Post tres dies resúrgam. Jube ítaque custodíri sepúlcrum usque in diem tértium, ne forte véniant discípuli ejus, et furéntur eum, et dicant plebi: Surréxit a mórtuis: et erit novíssimus error pejor prióre. Ait illis Pilátus: Habétis custódiam, ite, custodíte sicut scitis. Illi autem abeúntes, muniérunt sepúlcrum, signántes lápidem cum custódibus.
lectio5.eng: How far did the accomplishment of their diligent search reach? Even to the setting a watch of soldiers at the sepulchre, to guard the Lord, even after He was dead and buried. For they said unto Pilate: Sir, we remember that that deceiver (Matth. xxvii. 63.) This was the term by which they designated the Lord Jesus Christ, and the remembrance that He was so named is a sweet consolation to us His servants, when we are called impostors. So they said unto Pilate, that deceiver said, while He was yet alive: After three days I will rise again. Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest His disciples come and steal Him away, and say unto the people: He is risen again from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first. Pilate said unto them: Ye have a watch; go your way; make it as sure as ye can. So they went and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.

responsory5.lat:
R. O vos omnes, qui transítis per viam, atténdite, et vidéte,
* Si est dolor símilis sicut dolor meus.
V. Atténdite, univérsi pópuli, et vidéte dolórem meum.
R. Si est dolor símilis sicut dolor meus.
responsory5.eng:
R. O all ye that pass by, behold and see;
* If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.
V. O all ye nations, behold, and see my sorrow,
R. If there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.

lectio6.lat: Posuérunt custódes mílites ad sepúlcrum. Concússa terra Dóminus resurréxit: mirácula facta sunt tália circa sepúlcrum, ut et ipsi mílites, qui custódes advénerant, testes fíerent, si vellent vera nuntiáre. Sed avarítia illa, quæ captivávit discípulum cómitem Christi, captivávit et mílitem custódem sepúlcri. Damus, ínquiunt, vobis pecúniam: et dícite, quia vobis dormiéntibus venérunt discípuli ejus, et abstulérunt eum. Vere defecérunt scrutántes scrutatiónes. Quid est quod dixísti, o infélix astútia? Tantúmne déseris lucem consílii pietátis, et in profúnda versútiæ demérgeris, ut hoc dicas: Dícite quia vobis dormiéntibus venérunt discípuli ejus, et abstulérunt eum? Dormiéntes testes ádhibes: vere tu ipse obdormísti, qui scrutándo tália defecísti.
lectio6.eng: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch and anon, behold, there was a great earthquake, and the Lord arose. So great wonders were wrought about the sepulchre that the very soldiers, which were put to guard it, were witnesses thereto, if only they would have told the truth. But the same love of money which had made a slave of that disciple who was a companion of Christ, made slaves also of the soldiers that were put to watch His sepulchre. Some of the watch came into the city, and showed unto the chief-priests all the things that were done: and when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers, saying: Say ye, His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we slept. In good sooth, their diligent search had been accomplished and ended before this. What didst thou say, O stupid cunning? Wast thou indeed so utterly void of the light of godly wisdom, and confounded in the bottomless pit of thine own falsehood as to tell them to say: His disciples came by night, and stole Him away while we slept? Part of the testimony of thine eye-witnesses was that they were asleep at the time: thou thyself wast asleep not to be able to see that on their own testimony, their testimony must have been worthless.

responsory6.lat:
R. Ecce quómodo móritur justus, et nemo pércipit corde: et viri justi tollúntur, et nemo consíderat: a fácie iniquitátis sublátus est justus:
* Et erit in pace memória ejus.
V. Tamquam agnus coram tondénte se obmútuit, et non apéruit os suum: de angústia et de judício sublátus est.
R. Et erit in pace memória ejus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Ecce quómodo móritur justus, et nemo pércipit corde: et viri justi tollúntur, et nemo consíderat: a fácie iniquitátis sublátus est justus: * Et erit in pace memória ejus.
responsory6.eng:
R. Behold how the righteous dieth, and no man taketh it to heart; and the just are taken away, and none considereth. From the midst of sinners is the righteous translated;
* And his memory is in peace.
V. As a lamb before his shearers is dumb, so He opened not His mouth; He was taken from prison and from judgment.
R. And his memory is in peace.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. Behold how the righteous dieth, and no man taketh it to heart; and the just are taken away, and none considereth. From the midst of sinners is the righteous translated; * And his memory is in peace.

lectio7.lat:
De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Hebrǽos
11 Christus assístens Póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum non manufáctum, id est, non hujus creatiónis:
12 neque per sánguinem hircórum, aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.
13 Si enim sanguis hircórum, et taurórum, et cinis vítulæ aspérsus inquinátos sanctíficat ad emundatiónem carnis:
14 quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spíritum Sanctum semetípsum óbtulit immaculátum Deo, emundábit consciéntiam nostram ab opéribus mórtuis, ad serviéndum Deo vivénti?
lectio7.eng:
From the letter of blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews
11 But Christ, being come an high priest of the good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, that is, not of this creation:
12 Neither by the blood of goats, or of calves, but by his own blood, entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption.
13 For if the blood of goats and of oxen, and the ashes of an heifer being sprinkled, sanctify such as are defiled, to the cleansing of the flesh:
14 How much more shall the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?

responsory7.lat:
R. Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum,
* Advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
V. Quare fremuérunt gentes, et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
R. Advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
responsory7.eng:
R. The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together
* Against the Lord, and against His Anointed.
V. Why do the heathen rage? and the people imagine a vain thing,
R. Against the Lord, and against His Anointed?

lectio8.lat:
15 Et ídeo novi testaménti mediátor est: ut, morte intercedénte, in redemptiónem eárum prævaricatiónum, quæ erant sub prióri testaménto, repromissiónem accípiant, qui vocáti sunt ætérnæ hereditátis.
16 Ubi enim testaméntum est: mors necésse est intercédat testatóris.
17 Testaméntum enim in mórtuis confirmátum est: alióquin nondum valet, dum vivit qui testátus est.
18 Unde nec primum quidem sine sánguine dedicátum est.
lectio8.eng:
15 And therefore he is the mediator of the new testament: that by means of his death, for the redemption of those transgressions, which were under the former testament, they that are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
16 For where there is a testament, the death of the testator must of necessity come in.
17 For a testament is of force, after men are dead: otherwise it is as yet of no strength, whilst the testator liveth.
18 Whereupon neither was the first indeed dedicated without blood.

responsory8.lat:
R. Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum:
* Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
V. Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri, in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
R. Factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
responsory8.eng:
R. I am counted with them that go down into the pit.
* I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.
V. They have laid me in the lowest pit, in darkness, and in the shadow of death.
R. I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.

lectio9.lat:
19 Lecto enim omni mandáto legis a Móyse univérso pópulo: accípiens sánguinem vitulórum, et hircórum cum aqua et lana coccínea, et hyssópo: ipsum quoque librum, et omnem pópulum aspérsit,
20 dicens: Hic sanguis testaménti, quod mandávit ad vos Deus.
21 Etiam tabernáculum, et ómnia vasa ministérii sánguine simíliter aspérsit:
22 et ómnia pene in sánguine secúndum legem mundántur: et sine sánguinis effusióne non fit remíssio.
lectio9.eng:
19 For when every commandment of the law had been read by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
20 Saying: This is the blood of the testament, which God hath enjoined unto you.
21 The tabernacle also and all the vessels of the ministry, in like manner, he sprinkled with blood.
22 And almost all things, according to the law, are cleansed with blood: and without shedding of blood there is no remission.

responsory9.lat:
R. Sepúlto Dómino, signátum est monuméntum, volvéntes lápidem ad óstium monuménti:
* Ponéntes mílites, qui custodírent illum.
V. Accedéntes príncipes sacerdótum ad Pilátum, petiérunt illum.
R. Ponéntes mílites, qui custodírent illum.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Sepúlto Dómino, signátum est monuméntum, volvéntes lápidem ad óstium monuménti: * Ponéntes mílites, qui custodírent illum.
responsory9.eng:
R. After that the Lord was buried, they sealed the sepulchre, rolling a stone to the door of the sepulchre
* Setting a watch to keep Him.
V. The chief priests came together unto Pilate, and made that request unto him.
R. Setting a watch to keep Him.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. After that the Lord was buried, they sealed the sepulchre, rolling a stone to the door of the sepulchre, * Setting a watch to keep Him.

oratio_matutinum.lat: Réspice, quǽsumus, Dómine, super hanc famíliam tuam, pro qua Dóminus noster Jesus Christus non dubitávit mánibus tradi nocéntium, et crucis subíre torméntum:
oratio_matutinum.eng: O Lord, we beseech Thee, behold this Thy family, for which our Lord Jesus Christ was contented to be betrayed, and given up into the hands of wicked men, and to suffer death upon the Cross.

ant_laudes.lat:
O mors, * ero mors tua, morsus tuus ero, inférne.
Plangent eum * quasi unigénitum, quia ínnocens Dóminus occísus est.
ant_laudes.eng:
O death, I will be thy death; * O grave, I will be thy destruction.
They shall mourn for Him * as one mourneth for his only son, for the innocent Lord hath been put to death.

versum_2.lat:
V. Caro mea requiéscet in spe.
R. Et non dabis Sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
versum_2.eng:
V. My flesh shall rest in hope.
R. Neither wilt Thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

ant_2.lat: Mulíeres * sedéntes ad monuméntum lamentabántur, flentes Dóminum.
ant_2.eng: There were women sitting over against the sepulchre * weeping, and making lamentation for the Lord.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: In pace * in idípsum, dórmiam et requiéscam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: I will both lay me down in peace, * and sleep.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He shall abide in thy tabernacle: * he shall dwell in thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: My flesh * shall rest in hope.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Be ye lift up, * ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: I believe that I shall yet see * the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Dómine, * abstraxísti ab ínferis ánimam meam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: O Lord, Thou hast brought up * my soul from the grave.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Deus ádjuvat me, * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: God is my helper, * and the Lord upholdeth my soul.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: In pace * factus est locus ejus, et in Sion habitátio ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: His place is in peace * and His dwelling-place in Zion.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: I am as a man that hath no strength, * lying nerveless among the dead.

verses.lat: a Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus justítiæ meæ: in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
verses.eng: a When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

verses.lat: b Miserére mei, et exáudi oratiónem meam.
verses.eng: b Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer.

verses.lat: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
verses.eng: O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

verses.lat: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
verses.eng: Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

verses.lat: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: ‡ quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
verses.eng: Be ye angry, and sin not: ‡ the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

verses.lat: Sacrificáte sacrifícium justítiæ, † et speráte in Dómino. Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
verses.eng: Offer up the sacrifice of justice, † and trust in the Lord: many say, Who sheweth us good things?

verses.lat: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
verses.eng: The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: thou hast given gladness in my heart.

verses.lat: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui multiplicáti sunt.
verses.eng: By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, they are multiplied.

verses.lat: In pace in idípsum dórmiam, et requiéscam;
verses.eng: In peace in the selfsame I will sleep, and I will rest:

verses.lat: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe constituísti me.
verses.eng: For thou, O Lord, singularly hast settled me in hope.

verses.lat: Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
verses.eng: Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

verses.lat: Qui ingréditur sine mácula, et operátur justítiam:
verses.eng: He that walketh without blemish, and worketh justice:

verses.lat: a Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
verses.eng: a He that speaketh truth in his heart, who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

verses.lat: b Nec fecit próximo suo malum, et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
verses.eng: b Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

verses.lat: a Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus: timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
verses.eng: a In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

verses.lat: b Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit, (5a) qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
verses.eng: b He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; (5a) He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

verses.lat: b Qui facit hæc: non movébitur in ætérnum.
verses.eng: b He that doth these things, shall not be moved for ever.

verses.lat: Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. ‡ (2) Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
verses.eng: Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. ‡ (2) I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.

verses.lat: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra ejus, mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
verses.eng: To the saints, who are in his land, he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

verses.lat: a Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: póstea acceleravérunt.
verses.eng: a Their infirmities were multiplied: afterwards they made haste.

verses.lat: b Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
verses.eng: b I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

verses.lat: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
verses.eng: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

verses.lat: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
verses.eng: The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: for my inheritance is goodly to me.

verses.lat: Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
verses.eng: I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

verses.lat: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
verses.eng: I set the Lord always in my sight: for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

verses.lat: Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
verses.eng: Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

verses.lat: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
verses.eng: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

verses.lat: Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, † adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
verses.eng: Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, † thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

verses.lat: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: the world, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: et super flúmina præparávit eum.
verses.eng: For he hath founded it upon the seas; and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

verses.lat: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
verses.eng: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: or who shall stand in his holy place?

verses.lat: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
verses.eng: The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

verses.lat: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
verses.eng: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Saviour.

verses.lat: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
verses.eng: This is the generation of them that seek him, of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
verses.eng: Who is this King of Glory? the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

verses.lat: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: Who is this King of Glory? the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

verses.lat: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, quem timébo?
verses.eng: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?

verses.lat: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, a quo trepidábo?
verses.eng: The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.lat: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, ut edant carnes meas:
verses.eng: Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh.

verses.lat: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
verses.eng: My enemies that trouble me, have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

verses.lat: Si consístant advérsum me castra, non timébit cor meum.
verses.eng: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear.

verses.lat: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, in hoc ego sperábo.
verses.eng: If a battle should rise up against me, in this will I be confident.

verses.lat: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

verses.lat: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, et vísitem templum ejus.
verses.eng: That I may see the delight of the Lord, and may visit his temple.

verses.lat: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
verses.eng: For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

verses.lat: In petra exaltávit me: et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
verses.eng: He hath exalted me upon a rock: and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

verses.lat: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
verses.eng: I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: miserére mei, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: have mercy on me and hear me.

verses.lat: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
verses.eng: My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

verses.lat: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
verses.eng: Turn not away thy face from me; decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus esto: ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
verses.eng: Be thou my helper, forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

verses.lat: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
verses.eng: For my father and my mother have left me: but the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.lat: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
verses.eng: Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

verses.lat: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
verses.eng: Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

verses.lat: Credo vidére bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
verses.eng: Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

verses.lat: Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
verses.eng: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, et sanásti me.
verses.eng: O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, and thou hast healed me.

verses.lat: Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
verses.eng: Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.

verses.lat: Psállite Dómino, sancti ejus: et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
verses.eng: Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: and give praise to the memory of his holiness.

verses.lat: Quóniam ira in indignatióne ejus: et vita in voluntáte ejus.
verses.eng: For wrath is in his indignation; and life in his good will.

verses.lat: Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus: et ad matutínum lætítia.
verses.eng: In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.

verses.lat: Ego autem dixi in abundántia mea: Non movébor in ætérnum.
verses.eng: And in my abundance I said: I shall never be moved.

verses.lat: Dómine, in voluntáte tua, præstitísti decóri meo virtútem.
verses.eng: O Lord, in thy favour, thou gavest strength to my beauty.

verses.lat: Avertísti fáciem tuam a me, et factus sum conturbátus.
verses.eng: Thou turnedst away thy face from me, and I became troubled.

verses.lat: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo: et ad Deum meum deprecábor.
verses.eng: To thee, O Lord, will I cry: and I will make supplication to my God.

verses.lat: Quæ utílitas in sánguine meo, dum descéndo in corruptiónem?
verses.eng: What profit is there in my blood, whilst I go down to corruption?

verses.lat: Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis, aut annuntiábit veritátem tuam?
verses.eng: Shall dust confess to thee, or declare thy truth?

verses.lat: Audívit Dóminus, et misértus est mei: Dóminus factus est adjútor meus.
verses.eng: The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: the Lord became my helper.

verses.lat: Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi: conscidísti saccum meum, et circumdedísti me lætítia:
verses.eng: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:

verses.lat: Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar: Dómine, Deus meus, in ætérnum confitébor tibi.
verses.eng: To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not regret: O Lord my God, I will give praise to thee for ever.

verses.lat: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: et in virtúte tua júdica me.
verses.eng: Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.

verses.lat: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
verses.eng: O God, hear my prayer: give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
verses.eng: For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: and they have not set God before their eyes.

verses.lat: Ecce enim, Deus ádjuvat me: et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: For behold God is my helper: and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: Avérte mala inimícis meis: et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
verses.eng: Turn back the evils upon my enemies; and cut them off in thy truth.

verses.lat: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
verses.eng: I will freely sacrifice to thee, and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

verses.lat: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
verses.eng: For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

verses.lat: Notus in Judǽa Deus: in Israël magnum nomen ejus.
verses.eng: In Judea God is known: his name is great in Israel.

verses.lat: Et factus est in pace locus ejus: et habitátio ejus in Sion.
verses.eng: And his place is in peace: and his abode in Sion:

verses.lat: Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, scutum, gládium, et bellum.
verses.eng: There hath he broken the powers of bows, the shield, the sword, and the battle.

verses.lat: Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
verses.eng: Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills. All the foolish of heart were troubled.

verses.lat: Dormiérunt somnum suum: et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.
verses.eng: They have slept their sleep; and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.

verses.lat: Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Jacob, dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.
verses.eng: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.

verses.lat: Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? ex tunc ira tua.
verses.eng: Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? from that time thy wrath.

verses.lat: De cælo audítum fecísti judícium: terra trémuit et quiévit,
verses.eng: Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: the earth trembled and was still,

verses.lat: Cum exsúrgeret in judícium Deus, ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.
verses.eng: When God arose in judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.

verses.lat: Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
verses.eng: For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.

verses.lat: Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: omnes, qui in circúitu ejus affértis múnera.
verses.eng: Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: all you that are round about him bring presents.

verses.lat: Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, terríbili apud reges terræ.
verses.eng: To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: to the terrible with the kings of the earth.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
verses.eng: Lord, the God of my salvation: I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.

verses.lat: Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
verses.eng: Let my prayer come in before thee: incline thy ear to my petition.

verses.lat: Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
verses.eng: For my soul is filled with evils: and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

verses.lat: Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
verses.eng: I am counted among them that go down to the pit: I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

verses.lat: Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
verses.eng: Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: and they are cast off from thy hand.

verses.lat: Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
verses.eng: They have laid me in the lower pit: in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

verses.lat: Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
verses.eng: Thy wrath is strong over me: and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

verses.lat: Longe fecísti notos meos a me: posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: they have set me an abomination to themselves.

verses.lat: Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
verses.eng: I was delivered up, and came not forth: my eyes languished through poverty.

verses.lat: Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: expándi ad te manus meas.
verses.eng: All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: I stretched out my hands to thee.

verses.lat: Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
verses.eng: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

verses.lat: Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
verses.eng: Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: and thy truth in destruction?

verses.lat: Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, et justítia tua in terra obliviónis?
verses.eng: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

verses.lat: Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
verses.eng: But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

verses.lat: Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: avértis fáciem tuam a me?
verses.eng: Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: why turnest thou away thy face from me?

verses.lat: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a juventúte mea: exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
verses.eng: I am poor, and in labours from my youth: and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

verses.lat: In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
verses.eng: Thy wrath hath come upon me: and thy terrors have troubled me.

verses.lat: Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: circumdedérunt me simul.
verses.eng: They have come round about me like water all the day: they have compassed me about together.

verses.lat: Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: et notos meos a miséria.
verses.eng: Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: and my acquaintance, because of misery.

ant_vespera.lat:
Hódie afflíctus sum valde, * sed cras solvam víncula mea.
Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem, eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.
Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.
ant_vespera.eng:
Today I am greatly afflicted, * but tomorrow I will break my bonds.
With them * that hated peace I was peaceable: when I spoke to them they fought against me without cause.
From unjust men * deliver me, O Lord.
Keep me * from the snare, which they have laid for me, and from the stumbling-blocks of them that work iniquity.
I looked * on my right hand, and beheld, and there was no one that would know me.

oratio_matutinum.lat:
Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui Fílii tui resurrectiónem devóta exspectatióne prævenímus; ejúsdem resurrectiónis glóriam consequámur.
$Per eumdem
oratio_matutinum.eng:
Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God: that we who anticipate the resurrection of thy Son with pious expectation, may obtain the glory of the same resurrection.
$Per eumdem

oratio_2.lat:
Christus factus est pro nobis obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis: propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et dedit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen.
Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie. Et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui Fílii tui resurrectiónem devóta exspectatióne prævenímus; ejúsdem resurrectiónis glóriam consequámur.
$Per eumdem
oratio_2.eng:
Christ became obedient for us unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names.
Our Father, Who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: but deliver us from evil. Amen.
Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God: that we who anticipate the resurrection of thy Son with pious expectation, may obtain the glory of the same resurrection.
$Per eumdem

ant_3.lat: Príncipes sacerdótum * et pharisǽi muniérunt sepúlcrum, signántes lápidem, cum custódibus.
ant_3.eng: The chief priests * and the Pharisees made the sepulcher sure, sealing the stone and setting guards.

oratio_3.lat:
Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui Fílii tui resurrectiónem devóta exspectatióne prævenímus; ejúsdem resurrectiónis glóriam consequámur.
$Per eumdem
oratio_3.eng:
v. Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God: that we who anticipate the resurrection of thy Son with pious expectation, may obtain the glory of the same resurrection.
$Per eumdem

ant_1.lat: Dixit Dóminus * ad Adam: De ligno quod est in médio paradísi, ne cómedas: in qua hora coméderis, morte moriéris.
ant_1.eng: The Lord said unto Adam: * Of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, thou shalt not eat; in the hour that thou eatest thereof, thou shalt surely die.

oratio.lat:
Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
Per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen..
oratio.eng:
O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.
Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Thy Son, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen..

invit.lat: Præoccupémus fáciem Dómini: * Et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
invit.eng: Let us come before the presence of the Lord * and make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms.

lectio1.lat:
Incipit liber Génesis
1 In princípio creávit Deus cælum et terram.
2 Terra autem erat inánis et vácua, et ténebræ erant super fáciem abýssi: et spíritus Dei ferebátur super aquas.
3 Dixítque Deus: Fiat lux. Et facta est lux.
4 Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona: et divísit lucem a ténebris.
5 Appellavítque lucem Diem, et ténebras Noctem: factúmque est véspere et mane, dies unus.
